entries.title: The Missing Years: 2015-2019
entries.author: Chairman Rand Paul
entries.provenance: Publisher's cover and analysis printed on page 1 of the release (a scan, transcribed with macOS Vision OCR). Not one of the released documents.
entries.content:
The Missing Years: 2015-2019

EARLY-ONSET TRUMP DERANGEMENT SYNDROME. Before Trump took office, Dr. Fauci wrote he was "more and more concerned about even talking to the transition people

about being NIH Director since Trump is so unpredictable" (January 1-5, 2017). The day after the inauguration, he noted that

his wife marched against Trump in Washington and his daughters in Boston and San Francisco, and called the new President "amaxingly [sic] unpresidential!" (January 21, 2017). By March, the White House staff were "a scary bunch" and "Trump and his people are truly unscrupulous. This is outrageous!" (March 10-16, 2017). By 2019 he had a verdict: Trump "is acting more and more bizarre. Should be impeached, but Dems are rightfully concerned that this will galvanize his base

(January 1-7, 2019).

PUBLIC PRAISE. PRIVATE DOUBTS. When the World Health Organization declared its 2015 Ebola vaccine trial a 100% effective "breakthrough," Dr. Fauci privately wrote of "multiple flaws in the design and the analysis of the data" and a "terribly flawed study design." He went on CNN, BBC, and PBS anyway and told the New York Times the results were "very encouraging" and "impressive," noting in his diary that he had given a "congratulatory comment" while "slipping in the fact that the data, strictly speaking, are not statistically significant." His reasoning: "I am leaning heavily towards praise for the study. We cannot criticize the study since that is exactly what the press is looking for and then they will create a tension between HHS and WHO. HHS is too stupid to realize

that" (July 31, 2015).

RANSOMWARE ATTACK WIPED HIS CONFIDENTIAL FILES.

An entry from the summer of 2016 notes: "MISSING MATERIAL (Ransomware hack) ... will try to backfill." Dr. Fauci later

explained that his "entire unprotected folder" was encrypted and he "lost all of the letters that I have ever written as well as other important documents." The folder was created for "the confidential files that I made right after the anthrax attacks since I did not want them accessible to anyone." His verdict: "Bad idea!!!" (July 22, 2016).

"I CANNOT SEE WHY THIS IS SO SECRET." After being shown Senate Intelligence Committee documents on agents that induce cytokine storms "for which we have no countermeasures," Dr. Fauci noted that chasing every bioterror threat meant "fighting windmills" (November 22, 2017). After a "highest top secret level" classified discussion that China was "stealing our technologies for Ebola vaccines and therapies," he wrote: "I cannot see why this is so secret. This stuff is in the literature and in clinicaltrials.gov" (January 16, 2019). Presented with "believable intell" on foreign bioterror programs, he wrote: "I have heard this story multiple times over the years .... and they have never panned out" (March 26, 2019). Weeks before news of the COVID-19 outbreak went public, the National Security Council summoned him to the SCIF because of his "knowledge and standing and because I am Tony

Fauci" (December 6, 2019).

"BIG CHINESE VISITOR DAY."

Dr. Fauci hosted China CDC Director General George Gao at NIH ("Very smart and nice guy. Almost recruited to the VRC many

years ago"), then met China's Vice Premier, Health Minister, and the head of the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences at CSIS: "I gave brief description of activities of NIH in collaboration with Chinese" (September 27, 2017).

NOT JUST THE SCHEDULER

Patricia Conrad, Dr. Fauci's long-time special assistant, was not just keeping his calendar; she also attended high-level

meetings with him. She joined Dr. Fauci in the Dirksen office of Senator Richard Burr, then Chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, alongside ASPR Nicki Lurie, BARDA chief Richard Hatchett, Bob Kadlec, and Burr's chief staffer, as the Senator vented that he created BARDA and "now every time there is a global health emergency, we ask for emergency funds," and that the administration was "trying to steal from the BioShield account" (April 28, 2016).

Getting into the summer and ready for the IAS meeting in Vancouver. I have prepared very well for a talk of Comprehensive HIV prevention. Gave my almost-every-year talk to the St.Alban’s Summer School of Public Service. I talk on “my career as a public servant. Always fun. Enthusiastic students – high school from all over USA. Met with people from Gene Tech wanted to get NIAID interested in a product. Lobbyist was Tommy Thompson. Could not say no to them since it is Tommy whom I love. Great memories of when he was HHS Secretary.

Had teleconference in Building 1, Room 116 with activists who were concerned about the OAR budget (see above with Senator Cassidy). Also, they are not sure that Francis Collins will really fight to sustain the AIDS/OAR budget. Also, they are concerned now that Jack Whitescarver has retired, who will be the OAR Director. I have been convincing Francis that he really cannot decrease the AIDS budget to move money to other areas, even though deep down that is exactly what he wants to do. He is playing some politics in trying to ingratiate himself with the conservatives; however, in fairness to him, he does have a point about the disparity favoring AIDS research over others. On the call were Francis, Larry Tabak, Kathy Hudson, Jim Anderson, Bob Eisinger and activists → Mark Harrington, Peter Staley, Gregg Gonsalves, Mitch Warren, Lynda Dee, Jim Eigo, Kevin Frost (amFAR), Phill Wilson, among others. Friendly call. They really wanted a commitment to keep AIDS funding at 10% of NIH; however, Francis (with my encouragement) could not really promise that due to the ear-marks with NIH increases to other areas. However, I got Francis to agree that the scientific opportunities would dictate any increases in AIDS budget. Also, it would not get any smaller.

Met with Nicki Lurie, Lu Borio, Robin Robinson and Cliff Lane in 7A- 24 to discuss the ongoing situation in Guinea and West Africa regarding the ZMapp therapy trial and the Ebola vaccine studies. Cliff now up to >50 patients on the RCT for ZMapp. MSF still refusing to participate (they are against randomized trials even though the expanded/free access of Favipiravir and Brincidofavir have resulted in from nothing to disaster (toxicity). Also me with Slim and Quarraisha Karim in 7A-24. He wants NIAID support for a CAP256 (bNAb) trial in RSA. John Mascola was present at meeting since he helped make the antibody.

Griff Rogers and Josie Briggs will chair the Search Committee for the OAR. I met with them today to get them to understand that there is misperception out there that the OAR head will be the Chief HIV person at the NIH and as we know that just is not the case and so there should not be any unrealistic expectations when someone is applying for the job as to what their responsibility will be. Had dinner at my house with Charles Dinarello who was in town with one of his Dutch colleagues for a lecture. Charles has not changed a bit. He is wonderfully crazy, paranoid about not getting credit for his discoveries (he is correct since I believe that he should have won the Nobel Prize for discovering and cloning IL-1B.

Gave major lecture (on July 20) at the IAS meeting in Vancouver. Lectured on “Progress and Challenges in HIV prevention: Non-Vaccine and Vaccine Approaches”. Lecture went over extremely well. I could not help but reflect and comment in my lecture that 19 years ago, almost to the day, the first triple combination ART regimens with indinavir (protease inhibitor) + AZT + 3TC was presented at the 1996 Vancouver IAS meeting by Roy (Trip) Gulick and others. That was a transforming meeting since it began the era of HAART that turned around the field of HIV/AIDS. Now here in Vancouver, we see 15 million people on ARVs (largely through PEPFAR, Global Fund and others) and we are showing that you should start everyone at any CD4 count (START Study) and that Treatment as prevention (TasP – HPTN-052) really works as does PrEP. Another transforming meeting – 19 years later. On Tuesday (21 July) flew to San Francisco to have dinner with Ali. Saw her office at Twitter. She is doing great. Training for a marathon.

Had lunch at French Embassy with Professor Genevieve Chene of Viesan and Claire Aubin Counsellor at the Embassy and Mireille Guyader, Director of the USA INSERM Bureaus to discuss potential collaborations between INSERM and NIH. Beautiful few days in DC. Sunny, clear and no humidity!

Went to New Orleans today to visit Megan recently moved there after leaving Philadelphia. It was great to see her; however, it was oppressively hot. She is living in a really nice little studio apartment in a neighborhood just outside of French quarter. Stayed there until Sunday and flew back with Chris who had gone down one day earlier than I.

Went to dinner tonight at the Jefferson Hotel in the Wine Room as a guest of Catherine and Wayne Reynolds. It was the typical Catherine and Wayne social event with many interesting guess. I had the opportunity to sit next to Brent Scowcroft and we spoke about our common friend President George H.W. Bush. Brent is a wonderful elderly gentleman who has experience extraordinary times during his many years of government service. We spoke about the situation in Iran as well as in China. It so happened that the Chinese stock market lost about 10% of its value today, which is equivalent to a crash. Also at the dinner was Ben Carson who was running for president and who was taken to task by several people, mostly Democrats, at the dinner for his recent public statement that the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) was the worst thing to happen to the country since slavery. Ben then described his version of healthcare. He was getting blasted, and then I interjected and told him in front of the entire dinner table that although we have been old friends for a long time and that I respected his views even though I disagreed with many of them, his statement was in fact spectacularly unfair to the Obama administration. Several people at the table later told me that that was the most important thing that was said that night. Also at the dinner were Valerie Jarrett, Rick Atkinson, Eric Holder, John Negroponte, and an up and coming young African-American female lawyer named Angela Dry. Angela was particularly impressed with my statement to Ben Carson. Again, another terrific evening with Catherine and Wayne Reynolds.

Agnes Binagwaho, Health Minister of Rwanda, visited NIH and I went to her lecture in Masur Auditorium, met with her and her staff in my office and had dinner with her at La Ferme in Chevy Chase. We struck up a quick and warm relationship. I am pushing her (and she is responding as she feels the same way as I do) to truly try to end the AIDS epidemic in Rwanda. We will work together to develop a formula as to how to do that. She was accompanied by two young women (extremely accomplished already) who will start Harvard Medical School on August 2 and look upon me as a “legend”. They were delighted to meet me. Names: Kirstin Scott and Claire Wagner. They have been working for 1 to 3 years with Agnes as her personal staff. They are on their way to stardom.

Announcement of the “success” of the Ring vaccination trial for Ebola in Guinea made today by WHO. 17 infections in the delayed ring and 0 infections in the immediate ring. WHO selling this as a 100% effective breakthrough. Problem is that there are multiple flaws in the design and the analysis of the data that Phil Krause of FDA beautifully articulated. Bottom line is that we are dealing with an inherently good and effective vaccine that was put into a terribly flawed study design. And so now they (WHO, Norwegians, MSF) are claiming victory for the study, when it is the vaccine that could have proven effective in any study since it is so good. Such is life…. I gave congratulatory comment in the NY Times (Sheri Fink – reporter today) while still slipping in the fact that the data, strictly speaking, are not statistically significant. I appeared on CNN with Wolf Blitzer, BBC and PBS NewsHour. HHS COMMs (Leah Hunter) is getting all bent out of shape trying to micromanage what I say on TV and even tried to shut me down on TV but I appealed to Leslie Dach who gave me the go-ahead. HHS cannot decide whether they want to praise the study, give strong caveats or both. I believe that I am giving the right balance. I am leaning heavily towards praise for the study. We cannot criticize the study since that is exactly what the press is looking for and then they will create a tension between HHS and WHO. HHS is too stupid to realize that.

Appeared on CNN New Day this AM at 7:40 to discuss the outbreak of Legionnaire’s Disease in NYC (South Bronx) with 81 cases and 7 deaths. Outbreak related to contaminated cooling towers on the top of buildings. Reminiscent of the 1976 outbreak at the Bellevue-Stratford Hotel in Philadelphia. Again getting shit from HHS COMMS people (Leah Hunter) demanding “talking points” before she approves my going on TV, Radio, or Print. I am just going to go ahead without asking clearance. Also, just did CNN with Wolf Blitzer. Wolf was not there. Had a sub → Brianna Keilar.

Things in NYC still hot with the Legionella outbreak. Now there are 100 cases and 10 deaths. Gov. Cuomo calling in the CDC to the anger of DiBlasio and Mary Bassett (NYC Health Commissioner) since they feel that NYC can handle this themselves. Did CBS Radio News.

Media still hot for the NYC Legionella story. Staring to see friction between Governor Cuomo and Mayor DiBlasio in that Cuomo is calling for the CDC to come in (suggesting that the NYC health authorities are not responding well enough). Also, Cuomo is offering free inspection of all cooling towers on roofs. I appeared on MSNBC TV and CBS Radio (NYC).
Legionella still in the news. 113 cases and 12 deaths. I appeared on WTOP Radio with Mike Moss and Joan Jones at 6:40 AM yesterday (08/10/15).

DiBlasio and Cuomo have been criticized in the press for aquabbling with each other and are saying that the people wind up suffering when the authorities are fighting with each other. I appear on CBS News (NYC) about Legionella, but I do not get into the DiBlasio/Cuomo arguments.

Met today in my office with Dr. Mohamed Lamine Yansane the Counsellor for Piblic health in the Ministry of Health in Guinea and Professor Many Kader Konde, well known Guinean physician and president of Foundation Santi & Developpement Durable (FOSAD) in Guinea. Translation by Ydrissa Sow. Cliff Lane was present. They are in USA for meetings and were delighted to drop by. They praised Cliff for his work in Guinea and confirmed that Cliff was the only foreign health person who actually involved the host people in discussions before doing something in Guinea. They were “greatly honored” to meet me and want very much for me to visit Guinea.

Mark Harrington had sent me an e-mail asking to have dinner at a restaurant in DC since he and several activists wanted to discuss several AIDS issues including the search for the new OAR director to replace Jack Whitescarver as well as my recent talks on ending the AIDS epidemic and how they could help, at least in NYC or even globally. I suggested that we meet at my house and I cooked my famous Sausage and rigatoni with Caesar salad, Italian bread, appetizers (olives, dips, brie cheese) and Sicilian Pistachio and Coffee Chocolate Chip ice cream. Santa Margherita Pinot Grigio and Coppola Pinot Noir. The weather over the past several days has been gorgeous with Fall-like evenings. Unfortunately, tonight was muggy and it rained. And so we sat in the TV room for appetizers and went to the main dining room for dinner. Present were Mark Harrington, Peter Staley, David Barr, Mitch Warren, Moises Agosto, and Kenyon Farrow (Global Health head at TAG) and Carl Dieffenbach. Gregg Gonsalves was supposed to come, but he is at Yale and with the new school year starting, he could not come. Lively, friendly discussions. We reminisced some about prior dinners during the “years” of the activist movement at Jim Hill’s house. Interesting, that my good friend Peter Staley expressed concern that since I was 74 years old, what was going to happen to the field and the efforts when I retire. I told him not to worry since I will not retire for several years and/or until the epidemic is clearly on the way down. Of note, over the past few days the Stock Market has been crashing (down almost 2500 points in 1 week!!!) due to the crashing of the Chinese economy and the devaluating of their currency.

Stock Market stabilizing, but still now where near rebounding to the pre-crash level”. Had meeting in Medical Board Room (Room 4-2551) of Building 10 with the new OMB Associate Director for Health Programs Adaeze Akamigbo and her assistant Sarah Haile for a “meet and greet” to brief her on the NIH. At the briefing were Francis Collins, Larry Tabak, Kathy Hudson, Mitchell Goldstein of HHS, Doug Lowy and me. Key issue is that Francis used the opportunity to emphasize that he is against a 10% set aside for AIDS and that after re-reprioritization, he felt the AIDS allocation should probably decrease. He did not explicitly say that, but clearly he was hinting it. If the activists were in the room, they would have gone ballistic.

Had wonderful trip to San Francisco, then up the coast to Mendocino, then down through the Napa Valley to celebrate our 30th Wedding Anniversary. Ali joined us. When in SF, stayed at Bob Grady’s home at 15 Sea Cliff Avenue. First night in SF had cocktails at amazing rooftop bar called “Techo” with great view of the city. In Mendocino, stayed at a magical resort called Heritage House Resort with spectacular view of the Pacific Ocean and its cliff-like shores. In Napa stopped at Coppola Vineyard and Robert Mondavi Vineyard for wine tasting. Met Rick Ayre and Barbara Grady at the Mondavi Vineyard. Last night in SF went to the Mission district and had dinner at one of Ali’s favorite restaurants (broken down place, but charming.

Gave closing remarks at a ceremony at the White House (South Court Auditorium) to celebrate 25th Anniversary of the Ryan White CARE Act. Horribly hot (but sunny) day in DC. Waited on line for almost 1 hour to get into WH. Finally, people from NAPO had to “rescue” me and get me in more quickly. Speakers at ceremony were: Doug Brooks, Surgeon General Vivek Murthy, Jean Flatley, Tim Westmoreland, Henry Waxman, Senator Orin Hatch, Senator Joe Donnelly, Jeanne White –Ginder (Ryan’s mother) and 2 panels. Many AIDS friends were there including Eric Goosby, Jack Whitescarver. I spoke about the relationship of our attempts to end the AIDS pandemic and the important of the Ryan White CARE Act and program.

Gave Plenary Lecture at the Annual Meeting of the U.S. Conference on AIDS held at the Marriott Marquis on 9th Street and Mass Avenue, NW. Spoke on ending the AIDS pandemic. Large crowd of >1000. Very receptive to me – large proportion of gay men. Not the usual scientific crowd that I speak to – mostly community based people. Also on program was Nancy Pelosi, Doug Brooks and Kate Burton, Richard Burton’s daughter and Elizabeth Taylor’s step-daughter. here in DC when he visited a few years ago, but he was unquestionably my best friend at Regis. Brave guy. Taking it very philosophically.
Gepi Pantaleo in town for a day from Lausanne. Went to dinner at a different restaurant than the usual Café Milano. Went to Fiola Mare in Georgetown waterfront. Great meal. Good to see Gepi.
Went to Duke to give Keynote Lecture at Bart Haynes’s CHAVI-ID 10th Anniversary meeting. Spoke on “Ending the AIDS Epidemic with Non-Vaccine and Vaccine Prevention methods”. Quick trip.

Cliff Lane and I went to a small IOM meeting at the Keck Center (500 5th Street, NW) as a follow-up of the Hong Kong meeting that we (the USG) people missed because they called it without even consulting with us and then they realized that they did not have any senior USG people at the meeting. Tachi Yamada and Maria Freire chaired the meeting. Also present were: Nicki Lurie (ASPR), Ed Cox, Lu Borio, Phil Krause and Rob Califf (FDA), Beth Bell (CDC), Susan Sherman (HHS). Purpose was to try to reconcile some of the disagreements between us and the WHO (Marie-Paule Kieny), Wellcome Trust (Jeremy Farrar) that had surfaced regarding the conduct of clinical trials in West Africa with the Ebola epidemic. Meeting went well. We just firmly maintained that the USG (mostly NIH and FDA) would only be involved in clinical trials that are scientifically sound and that would come up with a scientifically defensible conclusion.

Attended Uplifting talking about his character Spt. 29, 2015 – Went to Baltimore to receive the “Lifetime Achievement Award” from Bob Gallo’s Institute for Human Virology. Other recipient was Nobel Prize winner Harald zur Hausen. Bart Haynes and Cliff Lane gave a very nice introduction of me talking about my character, accomplishments, etc. Good evening. Unfortunately, I developed except when I was receiving the award and giving my Keynote earlier in the afternoon (Adrenaline).

Participated in a panel for the Washington Ideas Festival (Sponsored by Atlantic magazine. Incredible cast of people – the entire “in crowd” in DC. I was on the panel with Vanessa Kerry (daughter of Joh Kerry) and the panel was moderated by NPR anchor Mary Louise Kelly. Topic was Global Health. Kerry was very gracious to me saying that it was a highest honor for her to appear with me. Following the Panel, I went to the Kennedy Caucus Room of the Russell Senate Building to observe the launching of the Kennedy Oral History Program. There was a speech by historian/author Michael Beschloss and a great panel chaired by Judy Woodruff and including Alan Simpson, Chis Dodd, Melody Barnes, Margaret Spellings and Barbara Perry. Got a chance to chat with Vicki Kennedy and Chris Dodd. Very moving remembrances of Teddy. Time well-spent.

Discovery Channel interview for big story on the NIH Clinical Center and the Ebola crisis among other issues. Spent 2 hours getting interviewed. Had telephone conference with Aftab Ansari (Emory) who has been doing the NHP studies with a4B7 in collaboration with us (Jim Arthos, Claudia Cicala, and me). The data are amazing for a potential “cure”. Cliff quite impressed. I will lead a clinical study of anti-a4B7 antibody in HIV patients treated with ART and undetectable viral load to then D/C ART and see if the anti-a4B7 antibody blocks viral rebound. Am making connections with Takeda Pharmaceuticals (who own the antibody). Mike Sneller and to some extent in a learning capacity, Kat Clarridge will execute the clinical trial. More later. This might be the real thing. We discovered the antibody and did all the subsequent studies over the past 7 years and most recently in the NHP in collaboration with Tab Ansari. Now others, Nelson Michael (Army) and Elena Martinelli (former fellow of mine and now in NYC) also want to do a clinical study. Only limited amount of antibody. I clearly have first right for reasons given above.

Was supposed to go to Laura Grady’s wedding in Charleston, SC. Has historic “Joaquin” Hurricane that gave massive floods (18 inches of rain). I cancelled but Chris went. The wedding was supposed to take place on a beach; however, this was impossible and so was moved to a mega-Church. Lucky that I decided not to go.

Went to MIT in Boston to take part in an event called “SOLVE” aimed at addressing and solving health problem throughout the world and domestically. Phil Sharpe invited me and Susan Hockfield (former president of MIT) chaired the panel. On my panel was Kiran Mazumdar (India), David Meeker (Genzyme), Mark McClellan (Brookings). At lunch at “The Catalyst” preceding the Panel, Rick Klausner and other notables were there. Good time. Got to Boston early and had coffee with Jennifer and saw her apartment in Sommerville for the first time. Beautiful place. Also, wonderful to see Lucca who was very, very happy to see me. Emerging problems with GSK over what adjuvant to use in the P5 HIV vaccine study in South Africa. They bought out Novartis who used MF59 (our original agreement). However, now that GSK has the protein (we paid for it) they want to do the study with their adjuvant (ASO1B). More later. I may have to meet with GSK chief, Moncef Slaoui to settle this.

Senate Appropriations Subcommittee meeting. I was not invited as a witness. Very strange. Suspicion of Jack Whitescarver (I had dinner with him last night) and AIDS activists is that either Senator Cassidy or Francis himself did not want me there since I defend the AIDS budget so well and Cassidy keeps talking about cutting it. Francis clearly wants to placate both Dems and GOP since he wants to stay as NIH Director after the elections (2016). Francis says I was not invited since the Senators said
Gave interview to Reid Wilson who is writing a book on lessons learned from Ebola.

Continue to work with Doug Brooks at NAPO, Kat Oakar, Amy Lansky Knowlton on getting the program going with Valerie Jarrett’s help to end the AIDS epidemic in selected cities (SF, DC, Baltimore. Oakland, Atlanta). Valerie is enthusiastic; however, she has made it clear that there is no new money for this project. We need to figure out a way to jump-start it with help of private organizations/ Cities/ States. At my suggestion we are also involving Jono Mermin (CDC) and Laura Cheever (HRSA). Had telepnone call with all of these today including Hilary Marston who has been very helpful to me on this. Also, I have consulted with Mark Dybul, Debbie Birx and Paul Farmer in this overlap with my efforst to help Agnes Binagwaho to do the same in Rwanda. Interesting conversation with Debbie Birx on Oct. 8 and she gave some caveats about Agnes as did Mark Dybul on a call on Sept. 18. They are saying that Agnes is using PEPFAR and Global Fund money to build up her health systems and is getting already 2x more per HIV case than any other Southern African country. They are very wary of giving her any more money. I hope that she is not “playing” me to help her get more when others have refused for good reason. I will keep an open mind.

Call with Mark Harrington who is concerned about Senator Cassidy’s attack on the AIDS budget at the recent Senate Appropriations subcommittee Hearing. Also, he definitely gets it and is suspicious why I was not asked to testify. He suspects that either Francis or the senators did not want my articulate voice advocating for AIDS. Went to book party/receiption for Jay Winik and his new book “1944 – FDR and the Year that Changed History” at Hay Adams Rooftop. Party given by Catherine and Wayne Reynolds and Rick Atkinson. The entire DC “A” list was there. Had nice conversation with Rick about how my book is coming. As usual, he was very encouraging of me. Many friends there – Nino Scalia; Fred Hiatt; Sen. Blount; Jane and Calvin Cafritz; saw Jan Donaldson for first time in a couple of years after her divorce from Sam; Lloyd Hand; Ruth Marcus; Howard Fineman (very complimentary to me); many others. Usual terrific time. Had leadership Forum today and afterwards Francis Collins met with me and several other Institute Directors to discuss the Senate version of the House 21st Century Cures Bill. Sen. Lamar Alexander (Chair of the Senate HELP Committee) wants his own legacy and so wants to put some mandatory funding for the NIH; however, he wants the money to be earmarked. This is an authorization bill and not an appropriations bill and so I believe this is an example of the authorizers wanting to make their own legacy by encroaching upon the appropriators’s turf. I am very much against earmarked money. I suggested to Francis that he insist in his negotiations with Sen. Alexander that they put into the bill a provision for some proportion of the money to go to investigator-initiated grants. Here again, Francis is pushing the agenda of “precision medicine” which is
Received nice written letter from Michel Sidibe congratulating me for doing the science that has helped us get to 15 million people receiving ARVs ahead of schedule.

Went to Yale School of Public Health (SPH) and received the Centennial C.E.P. Winslow Medal and delivered the Award lecture. The Winslow Medal is the highest honor bestowed by the Yale SPH. My lecture on “Ending the HIV/AIDS Pandemic: An Achievable Goal”. They gave me a prolonged standing ovation. Yale people tell me that is the first time in memory that anyone has ever received a standing ovation in that venue. Enjoyed very much meeting with and having dinner (ROIA Restaurant in Downtown New Haven)) with the faculty, pre-and post-docs. I was particularly struck by Alison Galvani a mathematical modeler epidemiologist who has written major papers on influenza, HIV and Ebola. She is a 38 year old named Chair Professor of Epidemiology at Yale. She looks like she is 18 years old. Real genius and very nice.

Few more Ebola infections in Guinea. Again and amazingly, MSF wants us to give them ZMAPP to administer to patients outside of the RCT. We cannot do this since we have been randomizing according to protocol all of our 65 patients including . MSF refuses to participate in an RCT. They are being in my mind unacceptably paternalistic by not giving the patient the choice of going on a trial or not. They are trying to play super-ethical by giving drug to everyone, and that in my mind can even border on unethical since we still do not know whether the drug works or not or is harmful.

Met with Cuban ministers of health in 7A-24. See WORD attachment for the names of the delegates. Hopefully, this will be a first step in developing collaborations with the Cubans. Cuban Delegation Bios and Institutions B
Appeared on WTOP Radio to discuss recent finding of statins decreasing the immune response to influenza vaccine among elderly (>65 years old).

Was the Keynote Speaker together with Michel Sidibe (UNAIDS) at a White House Conference on “U.S. Fast-track Cities and the National HIV/AIDS Strategy Meeting” hosted by Doug Brooks and ONAP. Went very well.

Off to NYC today to receive the “AID for AIDS” award tonight at Cipriani Restaurant (25 Broadway). Invited by Bill Haseltine. Had good time at the event tonight. Interesting crowd of mostly Hispanic-based AIDS advocates. Bill Haseltine’s 3rd wife is lovely (Maria-Eugenia). Got standing ovation after Bill presented the award to me. At the event, had long conversation with Nelson Cruz (Seattle Mariners) who wanted very much to meet me. Tony Danza was there presenting award to Danny Pintauro.

entries.content: Returned from NYC and was part of panel at the Dirksen Senate Office Building. Panel was Sens. Ed Markey, Bob Corker, Ben Cardin and Chris Coons; UN Deputy Secretary Ggeneral Jan Eliasson; Congressmen Barbara Lee and Jim Himes; Michel Sidibe and Fortunata Kasege and Deb Birx. In the evening, filmed a segment for the upcoming series on “The Eighties” produced by Tom Hanks for HBO.

Participated in a “Bipartisan Policy Center” panel discussion on PEPFAR held at the Newseum. Program introduced by former Sens. Frist and Daschle. My panel was chaired by Mike Gerson and Debbie Birx and former Finance Minister of Rwanda were on Panel. Good program.

Had dinner with Danny and Chris Hultzen at American Tap Room in Bethesda. Becoming a tradition now in our 3rd year. Caught up on Danny’s progress. He returns to Spring Training in January in Phoenix. This is last of his option years and so he either makes the team (MLB) or he gets waived. We discussed possibility of his becoming a relief pitcher since his arm gets fatigued after 50 to 60 pitches. What a great young man! I really hope that he makes it and fulfills his dream since I knew him as a 13 year old. After dinner with the Hultzen’s, I went with Chris to Georgetown to the Dog Tag Bakery upon invitation of Susan Axelrod. She insisted that I come even if I was late. There was a fund-raiser/reception/dinner for the CURE Epilepsy Foundation. Paul Simon was the guest of honor. He sang some of his hits (we did not get there in time to hear them); however, Chris and I had a wonderful 30 minute conversation with Paul. Susan and David Axelrod were extremely generous in giving us seats on either side of Paul. I was somewhat embarrassed since we walked in on them in the middle of their meal (they had just finished appetizers). Paul and Chris and I spoke about his career, his children (he was very proud that his son had just been admitted (early decision) to Brown, and his philosophy about the political situation (he had just had lunch today with Bernie Sanders). Apparently, Susan had told Paul all about me and he was very anxious to meet me. He is truly a gentleman and a very modest and warm individual. Great to meet him. Also at the dinner were Sylvia Burwell, Valerie Jarrett, Senator Al Franken, Lisa Monaco among others. Great evening!

Had dinner at the Home of the French Ambassador to the USA Gerard Araud. Dinner in honor of Dr. Christian Brechot, the President of the Institut Pasteur. Elegant affair. Went with Chris. All the many French there were excited to see me there. They all remarked about seeing me on TV all the time, etc.

Horrible terrorist attacks in Paris by ISIS killing more than 125 people. Bomb in soccer stadium where the President of France was watching the game (only few after approval from his upper management. We will put together a three page concept sheet for them to present to their upper management..

was called to the EEOB by Chris Kirchhoff to review a 55 page lessons learned document that was put together by the National Security Council. Big day today. It is World AIDS Day. Several important things happened today. I went to the White House, and as has been the case over the past several years I was asked by ONAP director Doug Brooks to give the main address at the ceremony in the South Court auditorium of EEOB. I gave a talk entitled “Ending the HIV/AIDS Pandemic: Follow the Science”. It was extremely well received and many members in the audience asked to have selfies taken with me. In addition, a blog that Chris Beyrer and I wrote for the CNN blog also came out today. In addition, the Huffington Post wrote a very complementary blog on my TEDMED talk. Prior to the meeting in the South Court Auditorium, Doug Brooks and I together with Carl Dieffenbach, Laura Cheever, Jono Mermin, Heather Hauck, Eugene McCray, Amy Knowlton-Lansky, met in the West Wing office with Cecilia Munoz (Director of the White House Domestic Policy Council) to discuss our test and link initiative that we (Doug Brooks and us) are putting together for five cities (San Francisco, Oakland, Baltimore, Washington DC, and Atlanta). Cecilia was very encouraging; however, as expected there would be no new money for this initiative. All in all it was a very good day. “VICE” did a show on HBO about HIV/AIDS for WAD and even though I was taped for over an hour, they did not show a single second of me. The producer later that evening wrote a note to Patty and apologized, saying they just did not have enough time. However, the show was terrible. They could not have done a worse job. Courtney wrote a note to the sub-producer expressing surprise and consternation that I was left out. Her boss, Shawn Smith called Courtney and profusely apologized saying that my general comments on the history of AIDS were extremely eloquent; however, when they put the show together, they did not fit well with the direction of the specific points that they wanted to make about cure and vaccine. He was mortified that they may have offended us. Oh well…..

Went to NAS on 21st Street, NW and presented my “vision” about where we should go with biodefense and emerging microbe research. John Holdren was present and was David Relman and others. My take was to develop generic platforms and broad spectrum diagnostics and therapies and NOT concentrate of chasing individual agents and stockpiling for them.

Went to Atlanta to deliver one of the Opening Keynotes at the CDC- organized National HIV Prevention Conference at the Atlanta Hyatt on peachtree. Spoke on “Ending the HIV/AIDS Pandemic: Follow the Science”. Three thousand people in the audience, many are community workers. Very well received. Also on program was Jono Mermin (Moderator), Doug Brooks (ONAP), Mindy Fullilove (Columbia), Eugene McCray (CDC). We are organizing the a4B7 concept sheet that we will send to Takeda to get upper management approval for our proposed clinical trial. Working with Cliff lane, Mike Sneller, Tae-Wook Chun, and Kat Clarridge.
Interviewed by GQ Magazine for a supposed “profile” on me. I suspect that the theme will be my clash with Senator Cassidy about AIDS research. We shall see how it turns out.

Another fabulous dinner hosted by Catherine and Wayne Reynolds at the Jefferson Hotel to honor Robert S. Langer of MIT (amazing inventor of medical devices, i.e. implantable birth control). Had “secret” teleconference in the Natcher Building SCIF connected with White House (Amy Pope – Ron Klain successor) + Nicki Lurie, Leslie Dasch, USAID people and also connected to CDC with Tom Frieden. Important meeting in person (my office) and by teleconference with the members of P5 to discuss moving forward with trial in RSA. Present in my office – Emilio Emini (BMGF), Larry Corey, Nina Russell (BMGF), Carl Dieffenbach, Rip Balou (GSK), John Siever (Sanofi), Hilary Marston, and GSK person over the phone (Marguerite). Had terrific Christmas holiday with my 3 daughters visiting with their dogs Sammy and Lucca. Did the usual Christmas Eve/birthday dinner over my sister Denise’s house. Back in action. Catching up with plenty to do. Zika virus and accompanying micrencephaly is rapidly spreading in Brazil with >3000 of microencephaly. I am writing a Perspective (hopefully to NEJM) with David Morens.

Took great trip to Monrovia, Liberia with Cliff Lane. We site visited the clinics and facilities that cliff has been working with over the past more than one year. We visited Redemption Hospital and JFK Hospital where we renovated the clinics. Also went to LIBR (Liberian Institute for Biomedical Research). Visited the U.S. Embassy and met with Ambassador Mark Boulware and DCM Sheila Parkman. Mark had just started 5 weeks ago; however, Sheila was great and was extremely helpful to Cliff throughout the conduct of the PREVAIL trials (Partnership for Research on Ebola in Liberia). PREVAIL 1 was the vaccine trials; PREVAIL 2 was the ZMapp trial and PREVAIL 3 is the survivor study. I also visited the CDC in the location of the embassy. I met with the CDC staff who had been mostly helpful to Cliff. Most of all I interacted with the staff that Cliff had put together over the past year. They were extremely excited to see me and I had an absolutely wonderful time interacting with them. I was deeply impressed with how run down the entire city of Monrovia was. I imagine the rest of the country is no better. It seemed that the homes were just one shack and shantytown type residents that were in extraordinary ill repair. I did not see any part of the city that looked like it was in good shape despite the fact that we drove around for hours from place to place. The Redemption Hospital which we have renovated was a broken down and falling apart structure. Apart from our renovated rooms it looked like a condemned building. I learned that the country still has not recovered from the Civil War which ended in 2003. There were many unfinished buildings that was started before the war and that just stopped during and after the war. This is a country that is in serious trouble. However I am told that they are making great strides and they are much better than what they were a couple of years ago. While we were in Liberia there was a secondary case of Ebola in a contact of the 22-year-old woman who died about 10 days ago. The trip was strenuous, but I did very well throughout. Zika virus situation is continuing to heat up. The CDC came out with recommendations for pregnant women who might be traveling to the involved regions. Unfortunately, they are a bit confusing since there is no real definitive and highly specific serological test that distinguishes Zika from dengue and other flaviviruses. The press interest continues and I will be on CNN tomorrow (Jan. 21) commenting on the progression of the outbreak and the disturbing number (now 3500) cases of microcephaly.

More attention to Zika situation. Did CNN New Day this AM and BBC taped for 5:00 PM slot and long segment for Brazilian TV – “TV Globo – News”. Also, interview with Time Magazine. Major Blizzard snow storm coming to DC tomorrow (Friday) and Saturday.

the situation with Zika virus is intensifying as the epidemic is beginning to explode in South America and the Caribbean, particularly in the North Eastern section of Brazil (Recife). It is estimated that there are over 1 million cases of Zika virus infection in Brazil and there has been more than a 20 fold increase in incidence of microcephaly in infants born of mothers infected during pregnancy. This is now gaining worldwide attention and I am being called upon more and more by the press to comment on the disease itself as well as on the preparation of NIH for the possibility that this will appear in the United States. The relationship between Zika infection in pregnant women and microcephaly in the fetus/infant is still an “association” and cause-effect has not yet been definitively established. I keep making that point. Of note, the CDC has now listed 22 countries where there is local transmission of Zika. These countries are in South America and the Caribbean. There is local transmission in Puerto Rico and there has been the case in the U.S. Virgin Islands. The CDC has put out guidelines that women who are pregnant, or plan to be pregnant should avoid travel to the designated countries until the situation gets clarified. They have also put out guidelines of what pregnant women who have been to the area and who may or may not have been infected should do. Also, a single case of very likely sexual transmission of Zika has occurred, which really complicates the issue for men who go to the region and return regarding the possibility that they may transmit the infection to their wives at home whom may be pregnant or about to be pregnant. In fact, the Brits will announce next week that they recommend that men who travel to the region use condoms for 1 month following return home. Also, a possible case of transmission through blood transfusion which led FDA next week to issue self-deferral guidelines for people travelling to the region similar to the situation with malaria for people who have traveled to malaria zones.

BEGINNING OF AN AMAZING WEEK!!!. I have been informed that there will be a meeting with the POTUS tomorrow in the Situation Room of the White House. Press interest continues and I have done much print press (NY Times, Washington Post, Reuters, AP, etc. as well as BBC radio and others.

appeared on the Diane Rehm Show with Maggie Fox (NBC) as the other guest in the studio and Scott Weaver calling in. Also did NPR radio with Rob Stein and multiple print media. Big event of the day was a one hour and 40 min. meeting with President Obama in the Situation Room of the White House (4:00 PM to 5:45 PM) to discuss the overall strategy to address the threat of Zika to the United States and our response to helping out in the Caribbean and South America. The agenda of the meeting was a dual presentation first by Tom Frieden through video link from Geneva where he was attending a WHO conference. I was in the Situation Room as the second part of the presentation concerning the research response to the outbreak. Present in the room among others were: Vice President Biden, Denis McDonough (Chief of Staff to the President), Lisa Monaco (head of NSC), Susan Rice, Sylvia Burwell, Shaun Donovon (Director - OMB), Valerie Jarrett, Gayle Smith (USAID Director), Heather Higginbottom (Deputy - USAID), Gina McCarthy (Director EPA), Jeff Zients (Economic Advisor), John Holdren (Science Advisor) . President Obama clearly wants to stay ahead of the situation and tasked us to come up with an immediate as well as a broad plan to address not only the current situation but future situations. He turned to me multiple times during the meeting for my opinion. When he spoke about addressing the immediate issue, Denis McDonough noticed that I was a bit uncomfortable. After the meeting, Denis stayed on and came over to me and told me that he has known me a long time (he was a staffer for Senator Daschle) and knows my body language. He picked up that there was something not completely right with my reaction to the President. In fact, I was concerned that when the President spoke about what he wanted to do, it was a little too focused on developing vaccines for Zika, dengue, and Chikungunya, as opposed to the broader plan that I thought he would want us to formulate. On the way out of the White House, Sylvia Burwell suggested that she connect Denis and me by e-mail so that we can chat by phone and clarify just what I felt should be done and how that aligned with what the President wanted. I came back to the NIH and set up a meeting with both intramural and extramural that might be involved in our response making it clear that this is an emergent situation and we have to put on a full-court press in doing what we do in the arena of research and development of countermeasures. Subsequent to the meeting with Obama, there is now a press fury about the situation. I have been given open clearance to talk to the press similar to what I did with Ebola. In fact during the meeting at the White House, Lisa Monaco and the President explicitly indicated that they wanted me on TV giving as much outreach and clarification and calming of the public with the evidence-based facts as possible.

And so the media blitz begins. I will list just some of the important appearances in addition to the countless print press interviews. I appeared this morning on CNN new day, ABC nightly news, CNN with Jake Tapper.

Am rapidly mobilizing my staff to respond with the research plan. I have made Hilary Marston the point person since already the workflow is becoming very intense. I am mobilizing John Mascola to pursue the DNA vaccine approach that leads to viral like particles, which was the one that we successfully used to bring a West Nile Virus vaccine into phase 1 trials several years ago. We did not take it any further since we could not find a pharmaceutical partner. I do not anticipate that we will have a problem finding partners because of the intense interest in this right now. In addition, we are putting out funding opportunity announcements to get the research community involved. Margaret Chan, director of WHO, has now made an announcement that Zika is a rapidly expanding pandemic that would involve "the Americas", as well as all of Africa, Asia, and southern Europe. She is clearly covering her ass because of the very slow and inadequate response of WHO to the Ebola outbreak. For example, today I appeared on CBS Morning Show with Norah O’Donnell, Charlie Rose and Gayle King, Fox Channel 5 TV, WTOP radio, NBC Nightly News, CBS Nightly News, BBC radio, PBS NewsHour with Judy Woodruff, Good Morning America with George Stephanopoulos, Charlie Rose - Bloomberg, among others. another amazing day!! Appeared on CNN new day and MSNBC Morning Joe. Then I went down to the Renaissance Hotel to appear at a longtime prearranged lunch at the Renaissance Hotel given by the Economic Club of Washington DC. This is chaired by my friend David Rubenstein, the CEO of the Carlyle group. David is also the President of the Kennedy Center. This is an event where he and I would get on stage after a luncheon and David would interview me about health issues in general. However, due to the furor of the Zika situation, there were dozens of reporters there and at least six television cameras recording the interview. We spent considerable time on Zika; however, we also discussed a number of other interesting health issues. The room was packed with a few hundred people, and the interview went extremely well. I am very impressed with David who is one of the great philanthropists of our time. For example, as a billionaire he gives away a couple of hundred million dollars per year. Most recently, he renovated the Washington Monument that was damaged by the recent earth quake. In addition he has renovated the Iwo Jima Memorial. He plans to soon do something with the Lincoln Memorial. Other press today included NPR Morning Edition. Another important event was the phone call that I had with Denis McDonough. Dennis explained to me that what the President really wants is to address this outbreak in the broadest sense in the context of what the effect of climate change, i.e. global warming, would have on our vulnerability to mosquito borne infections such as Zika, dengue and Chikungunya, among others. He wanted to develop a comprehensive plan but what we would do if years from now the southeastern part of the country becomes a semi-tropical region similar to Puerto Rico. Our response would involve everything from vector control to the development of vaccines for appropriate mosquito borne infections. Denis asked my opinion of how we could get this program started. I suggested that we get Sylvia Burwell involved in that she could utilize the office of the Assistant Sec. for Prevention and Response (ASPR). I e-mailed Sylvia and asked her to call me about this since Dennis is going to give this topic to Obama during their "daily walk" at the end of the day to bring up with Sylvia in his regular meeting with her that is scheduled for this coming Monday, February 1. It looks like I am going to get involved in another broad public health issue at the level of the White House.. In addition to all of this, Jim Kim, President of the World Bank called me asking for my advice and help in how the World Bank could help with the evolving Zika situation. He expressed the same concerned that he did with Ebola, i.e. that Margaret Chan and WHO as well as the people at PAHO are completely not up to the task of responding. He asked what I thought the most important thing to do right now. Once again, I emphasized that vector control is absolutely critical and that we have to put a full-court press on mosquito elimination and control in Brazil and other South American countries. Jim is very concerned that Brazil could experience an economic collapse particularly if the Olympic Games scheduled for this summer in Brazil are canceled because of Zika. He feels that if Brazil collapses, Argentina will follow and all of South America would be in dire straits. I suggested to him that he contact Sylvia.

Had long telephone conversation with Sylvia (Saturday - I believe she was at a soccer match with her child - maybe - noise in background). I gave her a heads- up for her meeting with the President on this Monday. Sylvia is a concerned that the President is putting too much emphasis on the effects of climate change and global warming due to the "Greek Chorus" of people in the White House led by John Holdren (Science Advisor) who keep pushing the climate change agenda. Sylvia feels they try to link it to health to give it more attention. She is showing wisdom and wants to make sure that the President understands that things like respiratory diseases spread by travel rather than by mosquitoes or other issues related to climate change are much more important than addressing the potential effect of climate change on the health of our nation. She will follow up with me after her meeting with the President. I am overwhelmed with work this weekend since I have to catch up with what I neglected (hundreds of e-mail among other things) because of this hectic week.

Got a text message from Senator Barbara Mikulski asking me to call her at home regarding Zika. She wanted a briefing on what NIH was doing, offered her help and also wanted some personal advice about her planned trip to Costa Rica.

Accompanied Secretary Burwell together with Tom Frieden, Gayle Smith and heath Higgenbottom to the Strom Thurman Room of the US Capitol to brief Senate Leadership on Zika. Intensity continues. More baby autopsies showing Zika virus in brain. Also, virus detected in semen in one person at 62 days. Quick trip to Stanford to give 1st Annual Leonard A. Herzenberg Memorial Lecture on Ending HIV/AIDS Pandemic. Extremely well received by a very sophisticated community. Gave long interview with Jon LaPook of CBS for weekend TV shows. Continuing with many calls/meetings on Zika. Had conference call with Secretary today regarding various roles of CDC, NIH, etc. Also, did Kaiser Family Foundation Web briefing for Press.

Presented a talk (Breakfast) at the Mellon Auditorium on Constitution Avenue and 13th St., NW on Ending the AIDS Pandemic at the “Alexandria Summit”. That afternoon was on a panel with Michel Sidibe (UNAIDS) and Deborah Birx (PEPFAR) on “Emerging Infections” at the Blair House. Got a nice tour of Blair House before the panel. Appeared on Brazilian national radio talking about Zika.

Had phone conversation with Jonathan Levine a film director who is directing a picture produced by and starring Amy Schumer. It is scheduled to be filmed in Puerto Rico and he was concerned about the local outbreak of Zika in PR. Although the risk is relatively low as long as the cast is not pregnant and not intending to get pregnant, the anxiety that I perceived they had about the location was intense. They have many women in their 20s in the cast and supporting personnel. They have the option of moving the filming to Hawaii. Given their anxiety and the real (although small) risk, I recommended that they move the filming to Hawaii. He was quite relieved that I recommended this. Went down to NAM/IOM to give a charge to the committee that HHS (NIAID/ASPR/FDA) commissioned to look at the clinical trials situation throughout the Ebola experience. Cliff Lane and I (and Lu Borio) were there. I passionately described my disappointment with the conduct of the WHO, Wellcome Trust and other NGOs (without specifically mentioning names). In particular, I mentioned how they were totally reluctant in cooperating with us in conducting randomized, controlled trials of vaccines and drugs, and they even said that randomized controlled trials were “unethical”. I pointed out that the open access distribution that took place during the Ebola outbreak led to learning absolutely nothing regarding what drugs are effective and whether they do harm EXCEPT for our randomize trial with ZMapp (PREVAIL 2). I also pointed out that the Ring Trial in Guinea also did not show statistical significance even though it is touted as being “100% effective”.

Newt: What do we need to be doing? The U.S. Government response to the Zika problem is focused at HHS with CDC taking the public health lead and NIH taking the biomedical research lead. This is a very serious public health problem that centers on pregnant women. Every week, the data are becoming more and more convincing that there is a truly causal relationship between Zika infection in a pregnant woman and congenital abnormalities and other adverse outcomes of pregnancy. A recent paper that came out online from the New England Journal of Medicine on March 5 (last Friday) showed the most powerful proof of causal link with 29% of Zika infected pregnant women showing fetal abnormalities on Doppler Ultrasound compared to 0% in the pregnant women not infected with Zika. This a disturbingly high attack rate. Now that we know that the virus can be transmitted by sexual contact from man to women, the threat broadens. Also, transmission can occur through the blood supply. Although it is unlikely that we will have a generalized outbreak in the USA, the threat of local outbreaks is real. We have seen this with dengue in Florida and Texas and Chikungunya in Florida. Clearly, we need a robust response to the outbreak. We need to understand the disease better with natural history studies and studies on pathogenesis. We need better diagnostics and importantly, we need a vaccine. I will start a phase 1 vaccine trial with one of several candidates at the end of the summer-early fall of 2016. I will start that by moving money from other important non-Zika projects. I will not be able to plan for the larger Phase 2 trial in 2017 without the supplement money. I need the money very soon if I am going to properly plan for that larger study. Tony and other colleagues: I am largely in agreement with you. I would like, though, to get a little bit of clarification. In PR, all that you say makes perfect sense and I completely agree with you (and frankly, with Don). But in thinking about this, I think there is perhaps an additional opportunity not to have to take full responsibility for the birth control situation ourselves as the USG. This is a risk and a situation that affects the entire community, and at the end of the day, caring for kids with microcephaly will fall to families and community members, likely without many more resources than they have now. This also means that it is a challenge that we, the federal government, cannot address without the entire community participating, including mounting a large private sector effort related to everything from clean up to screens to birth control and finding very different ways to enlist women of childbearing age in this response, including in choosing to delay pregnancy. In other words, success is about something much larger than individual decisions about pregnancy planning or lack thereof. I would hope that this kind of pretty dire advice could spur a different kind of action, in addition to being, I think, sound. That said, I think it is incumbent upon on to be able to articulate in advance how and why the situation in PR is different than what we are anticipating in CONUS, and to be clearer about what kinds of conditions would need to exist on the mainland for us to provide the same kind of guidance. I understand that transmission is becoming ‘widespread’ in PR, but being clearer about the threshold for ‘widespread’ elsewhere, will, I think be helpful. Finally, if I think back to H1N1, lots of people said that ob-gyns would never vaccinate pregnant women, and they did—furthermore, there has been a lasting impact. PR had few resources and so we will likely do better in this regard if we help out. Yes, we are going to enhance the birth control capability. I believe that we should state all of the above. However, I believe that we should also say that given the seriousness of the situation and the fact that we are expecting many cases of Zika infection in pregnant women in PR, and as a result many babies with congenital defects, women should at least consider where possible delaying pregnancy for one year or until we have a better feel for what the impact on PR will be this summer. I had to explain that BARDA is very successful in providing funds for countermeasures; however, the response to outbreaks involves more than producing and stockpiling vaccines/drugs/etc. It also involved all the surveillance and public health work of CDC. However, he was also upset that the language of the supplement request tried to change the purpose of BARDA by stating that it should be used for any public health issue that poses a threat at the same time that the administration is actually cutting money from BARDA and trying to steal from the BioShield account. He was not upset with me at all and we still are good friends. He is frustrated with the administration. Along the lines of the Zika supplement “wars”, Nancy Pelosi called me in my office tonight and asked if I would go to the Congress on May 10 and explain the importance of our needing the Zika supplement.

First death due to Zika in Puerto Rico, related to severe thrombocytopenia in a man in his 70s. Press interest continues in the diseases and in the budget battles. Did interview with a terrific person for radio and TV for BBC to air on May 5. Also did NBC Nightly News and MSNBC with Chuck Todd Met with Paul Stoffels (J & J; Janssen) together with Emilio Emini, Larry Corey, Nina Russell, Carl D. and Mary Marovich to discuss the funding and governance and design of the upcoming HIV vaccine trial with the human Ad26 /MVA boost to take place in South Africa. Good discussion. Paul is an old friend.

Had dinner with Catherine and Wayne Reynolds at Chez Francois in Great Falls, VA. Guests included Chris Grady, Francis Collins, Mike Morell (former Acting Director, CIA), Mary Beth Morell, General James Jones, Diane Jones. Many interesting conversations about Middle east, the Trump driven primaries, the likelihood or not of Hilary Clinton getting indicted for the e-mail situation. General JamesJones telling me how disappointed he is in Obama for relinquishing USA leadership throughout the world, including in Ukraine and especially in the Middle East. Mike Morell underscored this both essentially saying that Obama has been a foreign policy disaster. Interesting since they both served in the Obama administration.

Annual typical and wonderful Garden Brunch at given by Tammy Haddad, Hilary Rosen, Franco Nuschese et al. Since I have been on a lot of TV/radio of late with regard to Zika (see above), I was readily recognized by many of the movie and TV stars. Really good time meeting and having conversation with the usual DC people (Valerie Jarrett, Linda Douglas, Wolf Blitzer, etc) whom I always meet at these parties as well as Michael Kelly (Doug in “House of Cards”), Ian Kahn (AMC’s Washington’s Spies), Jaimie Alexander (NBC’s “Blindspot”). Had great conversation with Ian Kahn who felt passionately that if today’s politicians would ask before they act - :What would George Washington have done?” we would have a better country. Ian plays George Washington in a TV Series. He wants to reach out to me after the weekend. Also, ran into Jim Sciutto and his wife and other Regis High School grads (somewhat of a multi-generational reunion).

NAS Annual meeting. I defended dennis Kasper and Bart Haynes. Kasper did very well in discussion in section 44 (Microbiology); however, a few people in Section 43 (Immunology - Sasha Rudinsky and Emil Unanue) trashed Dennis for no apparent reason. Bart did well in Section 43.
Did very successful briefing on Zika at PAHO of the PAHO country “communicators” Many press there including 12 TV cameras from all over the Americas. Organized by Bill Hall from HHS.
