entries.content: Did Hearst TV and Fox 5 News on Zika. Went to NFID Dinner and Awards night to present Maxwell Finland Award to Diane Griffin (Hopkins) whom I nominated. Held at Bethesda Hyatt. Zika still dominating the news. Bad situation – Francis Collins notified John Gallin that he was essentially “fired” since the Red Team report recommended that NIH appoint a CEO to run the Clinical Center because of the issue brought up by the “investigation” by the team, i.e. inconsistent attention among some ICs for patient safety and FDA compliance with pharmacy and IV issues. NIAID did great in the evaluation, but other ICs did not. Francis is throwing John under the bus on this one. The Red Team led by Norman Augustine was called in by Francis to investigate the issue of the conditions (that came to light last May – 2015) in the CC Pharmacy with compounding experimental drugs. No patient was hurt but it was clear that in an attempt to service investigators, the pharmacy did not abide by strict GMP practices, particularly in the physical structure of the pharmacy modules. Two vials were found with precipitate in them and the Pharmaceutical Development Branch was closed. The FDA investigated and was not pleased at first with the response. Meanwhile the “Red Team” did a broad look at the CC and found a culture of caring more for research than for the patients (not at NIAID, but in other ICs). One thing led to another and the recommendation was to appoint a CEO for the CC, which in effect eliminates John Gallin. There is some truth in the inconsistencies in care among the ICs; however, John Gallin was never given the authority to do anything about it. Yet, he is being blamed. It is up to the ICs to demand excellence. John is a bit at fault since he has been very passive in demanding (even though he did not have the authority) that the ICs do better. Francis is also at fault since he never gave the CC the resources to have a pharmacy or other facilities that are up to today’s standards. NIH Record New Oversight Coming to C `

Amazing weekend at Ohio State University for the Commencement Address. I spoke in the Ohio Stadium in front of 70,000 people!!. My talk went extremely well. There were initial tweets over the prior couple of weeks and write-ups in the school papers about “mixed feelings” among students that they got a “relatively unknown” personality to be commencement speaker instead of a celebrity comedian or movie star. Last year they had Obama. Some students said that they had looked me up and found that my accomplishments were amazing and they were interested in what I had to say. Others expressed disappointment that I was not a celebrity. That all changed after the address. The enthusiasm for me was amazing. All the tweets praised me as did the school newspapers. I was mobbed as I left the stadium by hundreds of students and parents who want to shake my hand, touch me, take “selfies’ with me. This continued at the airport where literally hundreds of people came up to me to congratulate and praise ny talk. Amazing weekend!

Went to NYC for a DDCF Board meeting. Got there early to do an interview with the Editorial Board of BuzzFeed located on East 18th Street. Beautiful sunny day. I enjoyed walking around Union Square and then realized that I was near Larry Kramer’s apartment on , right near Washington Square Park. I spontaneously dropped in on him (Apartment ) and had a great chat. He was thrilled that I visited him. Had pre-brief with Sylvia Burwell by phone in preparation for our lunch meeting tomorrow with the Editorial Board of the Washington Post. Sylvia called me back afterwards and expressed concern about the CDC was handling the Zika issue. Sylvia does not trust their judgment and competence based on her experience with Ebola.

Did interview on NPR – “Morning Edition” with Renee Montagne on Zika to be aired tomorrow.

Article came out in Washington Post by Lena Sun describing on the Red Team’s report. Very damaging to NIH. NIH community vey angry with Francis Collins for essentially allowing this in order to cover his ass. Gallin is the sacrificial lamb. Francis announced that the NIH will have CEO, COO and CMO and the Gallin will have to step down, i.e. John was fired. Did great on camera interview on Facebook and Online for USA Today with senior editor Susan Paige. Continued back and forth in Congress regarding the $1.8 billion request for Zika. I will testify tomorrow before the House in a special briefing areranged by Nancy Pelosi.

My picture was in USA Today and I was prominently mentioned in a Washington Post Editorial and a NY Times Editorial. Anne Schuchat, Mitch Landrieu (Mayor of New Orleans) and I briefed the Democratic Steering Group for Zika in The Capitol Visitors Center at 1:00 PM<. Chaired by Pelosi with Nita Lowy, Rosa DeLauro, etc. 35 Members present. Great hearing. Love fest for me by my old friends (Pelosi et al). Did TV interview for the ABC World News Tonight. Francis Collins wants my help in trying to fashion something for John within the Clinical Center that would be acceptable to him. Francis obviously realizes the unpopularity of his action to remove John as Clinical Center Director. I will come up with some options.

See e-mail below: RE More thinking about JG.msg
Media coverage still intense. Did Fox Cavuto Show today. Also, many quotes in numerous blogs and print news. Will have dinner tomorrow night with John Gallin to try and help.

Dinner with John and Elaine Gallin. John feels that he is being set up for failure. Francis wants him to stay on after he has essentially fired him by announcing that he is bringing in a CEO. I am trying to fashion a position in the Clinical Center where John could function as the “Scientific Director” of the CC research programs of the various CC departments. John will consider this.

Did MSNBC show on Zika. Also, attended the IOM (NAM) meeting at the NAS on Vaccines for emerging infections. Gave opening talk on the need for establishing flexible vaccine platforms. Meeting chaired by Adel Mahmoud and Marie- Paule Kieny with Victor Tzau as the host.

Went to NYC today to receive the “Chivalry Award” from the American Foundation of Savoy Orders, a 1000 year old Italian Organization of knighthood. Received it at a beautiful townhouse at . Chris was with me. Out to dinner after with Chris and Phil Piccigallo.

Gave CEO Luncheon lecture at the Army-Navy Club at Farragut Park on 17th Street, NW. Also, this evening participated in a telebriefing for the constituents of Congresswoman Deborah Wasserman-Shultz (D-FL), which she moderated. Did it with Steve Redd (CDC). There were over 2000 call-ins on the phone. Went very well. May 20, 2016 – Big day! Briefed President Obama in the Oval Office from 11:00 AM to 12:20 PM. Tom Frieden, Secretary Burwell, and I did a combined briefing. I spoke predominantly about Zika vaccines and Tom handled the public health issues. Present at the briefing were VP Joe Biden, Celia Munoz, Valerie Jarrett, Amy Pope, Susan Rice, Shaun Donovan (OMB), and Amy Rosenbaum (WH legisl). Also, sat in (without comment) on the Press conference that the POTUS held in the Oval Office right after the briefing. Went very well. POTUS very familiar with me, Tom and what we are doing.
(Sunday) – Appeared on ABC This Week with George Stephanopoulos to discuss Zika and my recent visit to the oval office with Obama.
Delivered Commencement Address at Yale University School of Medicine. Went extremely well. Nice discussions with Jerry Friedland and Alison Galvani.

Went with Francis Collins to the Capitol to do a meet and greet with a number of Republican and Democratic Congressmen set up by Pete Sessions (R-TX). They mostly asked about Zika and I held forth. Tim Murphy, Mike Burgess, Fred Upton, Rosa DeLauro, etc. Interesting that Congressman (Dr.) Burgess was insisting that I recommend to Obama to restrict travel for anyone to Zika areas, not just pregnant women. He was not alone in this feeling. I was surprised since Mike is an old friend and a good guy. Went to Wilson Center and participated in a Zika Panel chaired by Jane Harman and Moderated my Jason Beaubien of NPR. On panel - me, Anne Schuchat, and former Congresswoman Susan Molinari. Jane and Susan were very, very complimentary of me for my “decades of amazing work on public health”. Went with Bob Seder to Mets game. Many home runs – Zimmerman, Rendon, Revere, Murphy, Ramos. Francis Collins sang National Anthem!!
Press continues – appeared on CNBC “Squawk Box”. Also, did KTSA radio from Texas. NPR from Houston and NPR from Miami.

Attended Annual Sons of Italy Gala at the Building Museum. I received the Lifetime Achievement Award here last year. This year Condoleezza Rice received the award. She sat at our table with Phil Piccigallo and the Italian Ambassador to the USA – Claudio Bisogniero. We reminisced about out shared interactions (PEPFAR, etc.) during the Bush 43 White House years. Joe Montegna was Master of ceremonies and Gary Sinese was special guest.

Press continues with Zika. Also, report of mcr-1 gene (resistant to Colistin) in an E.coli in a woman in Pennsylvania. Press continues → CNN; Wall Street Journal; Bloomberg TV; “Environmental Health perspective” published by NIEHS; Steele and Ungar Radio Show.
(Memorial Day weekend) Did CNN NewDay on Zika and MCR-1 gene bacterial resistance.

Much media today on Zika as well as MCR-1 gene found in an E.coli in a woman in Pennsylvania. This gene leads to resistance to colistin (last line drug) - WTOP radio on Zika and MCR-1; also did CNN NewDay again. Also, did Reuters TV; Katy Kay at BBC TV; NY Times interview; MSNBC with Chris Hayes

Honduran pregnant women infected with Zika in Honduras comes to USA on vacation and delivers a microcephalic baby in Hackensack, NJ I do MSNBC with Andrea Mitchell; NBC Nightly News. MISSING MATERIAL (Ransomware hack) – June 2 through July 13, 2016 – will try to backfill

Went to NYC to the UNSpecial Session on HIV/AIDS and presented in a panel with Michel Sidibe and Deb Birx on how we can end the AIDS pandemic. I gave my usual talk on the scientific basis for the feasibility of doing this. “We have the tools….”.

Briefed the democratic Steering and Outreach Committee in the Mansfield Room of the US capitol together with Sylvia and Tom Frieden on an update of Zika and why we desparately need the money. Received President’s Award from the President of Georgia (given by the Ambassador) on the celebration of the 25th Anniversary of the independence of the country of Georgia. It was held on the rooftop terrace across from the capitol.
Continue to do press virtually every day on Zika. Did CNN TV this evening.
Did Zika briefing at the White House for Community people in EEOB 350.

Did a meet and greet with mostly GOP House members in Room H-314 (Rules Committee) of the Capitol. Meeting called by Rep. Pete Sessions of Texas. Good “back and forth”. Francis Collins and I. Most discussion about Zika.

Did Aspen Ideas Festival. Was on Zika Panel with Anne Schuchat and Rob Califf, chaired by Jeff Goldberg of The Atlantic. Also did panel on drug development chaired by Helen Branswell of STAT. really enjoyed the trip!
Had beautiful reception at the Canadian Embassy in my honor for receiving the Gairdner Global Health Award. Many friends from NIH and elsewhere attended. Also, Denise and Jack, Joanne and Jim, etc.

Meet with the POTUS in the Oval Office of the White House together with Tom frieden and Sylvia Burwell to update him on the Zika situation. The Congress has still not appropriated the money for Zika that the POTUS has requested ($1.9 billion) and there is a pissing match back and forth between the Dems and the GOP regarding the funding. The GOP want to give the money but with “poison pill” provisions such as taking the money from the Affordable Care Act and from the Ebola account and they want to unfund Planned Parenthood. The Dems reject this and the Congress will leave for their 4th of July break without acting

Much press exposure for me virtually every day associated with Zika and my explaining the need for money for vaccine, etc. Congress leaves for the Convention and for the summer break without an Zika Appropriations. The press are pounding them (mostly the GOP) for playing politics with a public health crisis.
60 Minutes did filming here at VRC on Zika and took footage to do a profile on me in the future.

Trip to Durban, South Africa for the 21st International AIDS Society (IAS) meeting. Gave Keynote at the CURE Symposium; received the President’s Award from the IAS. Great meeting. Much praise and recognition. Now have 2nd person in Florida with local transmission of Zika!! – a male with no possibility of sexual transmissions to him; first person a few days ago was a 23 yo pregnant woman. Had important phone call at 9:00 PM with HHS Secretary Burwell, Tom Frieden, me and others from HHS on how we will handle the contentious issue of potentially doing a travel alert for Florida for pregnant women, which would trigger the questions of what do you do with pregnant women who live in the Florida region. State authorities, particularly Texas are very upset about the possibility of CDC issuing a travel alert for their state. As usual, Sylvia Burwell either e-mails or calls me after the conference calls and seeks my independent counsel regarding sensitive policy issues.

I was attacked by “Ransonware” and my entire unprotected folder (C Drive – Word Files) was encrypted. Luckily, I had a backup of most of my historical daily notes and my autobiography was on a separate, nonaccessible folder. However, I lost all of the letters that I have ever written as well as other important documents in the Word Files folder. I had originally created this folde for the confidential files that I made right after the anthrax attacks since I did not want them accessible to anyone. However, I soon began putting other important documents into that folder – Bad idea!!!

Continuing to do much “local” media (local TV and Radio stations as well as local NPR stations) set up by HHS to update on Zika and continue to pressure the Congress (which has not recessed for the summer) to appropriate the money for Zika. Democratic Convention this week. Michelle Obama gave an amazing speech endorsing Clinton. She spoke about her children and their future in America. Bill Clinton also gave a great speech “humanizing” Hillary.

Great speeches at Dem Convention by VP Joe Biden and Obama. Still doing Zika press. Much local press given the local transmitted cases in Florida: NPR Radio in California – KNX radio; ABC – KSAT Kansas (TV); WMBF – TV – Myrtle beach; WAMC radio Albany.

As predicted, it is happening! Two more local transmitted cases (total = 4, at least) in Florida. FDA ordering no blood collections for transfusion in Dade and Broward Counties until they can implement blood screening. I taped for tonight PBS NewsHour and NBC Nightly News. Continue local media: KJZZ Radio – NPR; WRC NBC local with Doreen Gentzler

Now confirmed total of at least 4 local transmission. Governor Scott from Florida confirms. Much discussion here at HHS regarding if/when to issue a travel alert to pregnant women not to travel to Miami-Dade and Broward Counties where local infections are. Continue to do local media: WSVN TV Miami; KNBC TV – Los Angeles; WINA Radio – Charlottesville; Radio KSTX – San Antonio; Also did CNN with Wolf Blitzer. Also, did BBC TV via phone where they showed my picture on the screen. Also, on reviewing data I realize that we should probably be doing an Alum Adjuvant arm to the HVTN 702 trial in addition to the MF59 adjuvant arm. Looking at data from Feffa Franchini (NCI), she found that in a NHP model to reproduce RV144 in the monkey, she found that MF59 arm did not protect, whereas the Alum arm did. Also, both arms gave the important antibody against V2 (the key cyclc dipeptide), while MF59 also gave response to V1. Could be that although MF59 is a more potent adjuvant than Alum, it induces an antibody response (against V1) that hinders the protective effect of the alum limb. I will convene the HVTN 702 group to discuss adding an Alum arm to the trial in Africa.

Spoke over the phone with Carl Dieffenbach, Larry Corey, and Bart Haynes about the issue with Feffa’s study and HVTN 702. Spoke (as usual) with Tom Frieden by phone. He is frustrated by the fact that that HHS and Secretary Burwell seem to distrust the CDC and Tom and continually micromanage them. He is partially correct since HHS (Sylvia) often calls me to validate what Tom tells them.

(Sunday)– Appeared on Sunday AM “Face the Nation” talking about the locally transmitted cases of Zika. Show went extremely well. One of the best that I have done. John Dickerson has now evolved into one of the best Sunday Show hosts. I predicted that there would be more cases soon and that we would not hesitate to declare a travel alert for pregnant women to the area in the restricted region inside Dade County. I found out from Tom Frieden after the show that there wer now additional symptomatic and asymptomatic cases (total 14) within that restricted area. Together with the Florida Health Authorities, we will issue a travel alert for pregnant women for this restricted area. Testing is going on around the “rim” of this area. I suggested to Tom that we add a cushion rim of restriction now. He wants to wait until we test the rim (tomorrow) before we do this. The Florida health authorities will go nuts if we issue an alert for the entire Dade County that includes Miami. It would destroy tourism even if it is only an alert for pregnant women. England has already issued a travel alert for pregnant British women for the restricted area. I am not concerned about the tourism. If there are cases around the rim tomorrow I will push for widening the restriction. Big conference call at 3:00 PM with Secretary Burwell to discuss situation. We are having a terrible heat wave (>20 days in July >90 degrees F). NY Times Sunday article on Obama being a science nerd. Had me quoted about his visit to nancy Sullivan’s lab in the VRC and how he addressed the scientific community in Masur auditorium and blew the audience away with science talk. Article by Gardiner Harris.

Did CBS Morning News with Charlie Rose and WTOP Radio on the evolving Zika situation. Gov. Scott of FL announces the new cases (6 additional found by Uro-screening of asymptomatics + others) – total of 14. Calls for help from CDC Emergency Response Team. Mentions that CDC will issue travel alert for pregnant women to the restricted area north of downtown Miami. CDC to announce travel restriction at 1:00 PM. As a result → Press requests starting to role in. Did MSNBC with Andrea Mitchell; also did NBC Nightly News; CBS Evening News and CNN with Jake Tapper; BBC Radio; This amazing article by Laurie Garrett appeared in Foreign Policy on August 1, 2016 Dear Washington: The Time to Prepare for Zika Has Come and Gone Act now, or bear the blame for the virus's devastating effects. • By Laurie Garrett • August 1, 2016

Dear presidential candidates, senators, and congressional representatives: Get your butts back to Washington immediately. The time you’ve had to get a preparedness plan in order but have wasted twiddling thumbs and shifting around budgets to make it look like you were taking the threat of Zika seriously is over. So, go behind closed doors to negotiate if the glare of the media and prying eyes of your constituencies is uncomfortable — I don’t care. But know this: The goal is to prevent a major pandemic from sweeping the nation, the births of thousands of Zika-deformed and neurologically impaired babies, to forestall adult cases of Guillain-Barré syndrome, eye problems, and other rare disorders caused by Zika infection, as well as to prevent the devastation of other public health and safety programs in cities, counties, and states across America as they shift resources from one account to another. If I were the referee for your negotiations — which ought to commence this week in light of Florida’s local mosquito-carried Zika cases — the allowable focus for partisan debate between the houses of Congress and the White House would be extremely narrow. I would rule everything from the future of Planned Parenthood to pesticide regulations, shifting money from Ebola responses and existing federal and state accounts, the budget deficit, national debt — all off the table. The one, and only, topic open for debate? How much new money must be allocated on an emergency basis to meet the needs of the nation’s scientists, public health leaders, hospitals, maternal health providers, and mosquito and environmental health experts in order to limit the number of Americans who fall ill to Zika, pass the virus sexually to their partners or in utero to their fetuses, miscarry, or are born with neurological deficits and deformations. Your mandate starting now: Show me the money. Partisan bickering about the lives of American babies is unconscionable. This is no time for grandstanding. As of Aug. 1, 161 days have elapsed since the White House requested $1.9 billion in emergency funds for Zika, met by various counterproposals from the House and Senate Republican leaderships. That’s 161 days during which researchers and public health experts have struggled, with no new resources of any kind, to figure out how the virus works, find ways to control it, work on vaccines and treatments, and develop effective mosquito-control tactics. If, politicians, you truly care about the right of every baby to a healthy life, you have no excuses, no rationales, and, yes, you will pay a price in upcoming elections if you fail. I don’t personally care whether you are Democrat or Republican, and neither will the voters living in regions that get slammed by the virus. The only question pregnant women, worried that they might be carrying a severely deformed child, will be asking is this: What did you do in the first week of August, once Zika was in Floridian mosquitoes, to protect my family from the newly arrived birth-defect-causing virus? And here’s the thing: Americans aren’t stupid and won’t be hornswoggled. According to recent polls, most people in the United States know what Zika is and were concerned about it well before the virus infected Floridian Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. We have, as a nation, watched the epidemic reach our shores in slow motion, starting in mid-2015 when the Brazilian government issued its first announcements about babies born with microcephaly — literally, squashed brains and misshapen skulls. Six months ago, on Feb. 1, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a global Zika emergency. Americans looked south throughout our winter as the infected mosquitoes popped up across most of South America, Central America, and the Caribbean and as cases of microcephaly and other tragic disorders mounted. Shortly after Florida’s governor, Rick Scott, announced on Friday that four people in Miami had contracted Zika from local mosquitoes, the nation’s most venerated epidemic scientist held his own press conference in Washington. Anthony Fauci, who has directed the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases for more than 30 years, soberly said that “we are watching a pandemic in process” and that he was “almost certain that we will see more cases across the United States.” On Monday, Scott confirmed 10 more homegrown cases of Zika in Florida. And the rob-Peter-to-pay-Paul approach Fauci’s agency has had to use for 161 days in order to conduct Zika research in the absence of emergency funding? “We are getting to the point very, very soon that we are going to run out of the money that we are borrowing from ourselves,” Fauci said in a Friday briefing at the Bipartisan Policy Center in Washington. You should pay heed to Fauci — this man has a long and storied track record on epidemics. He has been running the NIAID longer than anybody has ever directed any of the nation’s major scientific institutions, starting in the early 1980s when a mysterious form of cancer and lung disease was cropping up among gay men — that turned out to be the dawn of the AIDS pandemic. And it was Fauci who warned Presidents Ronald Reagan, George H. W. Bush, and Bill Clinton that all three presidencies were failing to grasp the scope, severity, and urgency of AIDS. The first president to take Fauci seriously was George W. Bush, who created the multibillion-dollar President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), which today is credited with dramatic reductions in HIV deaths all over the world. But the Brooklyn-born scientist who has given his entire career to public service wasn’t just right about HIV; Fauci has correctly advised five presidents and hundreds of members of Congress about SARS in China, the 2009 bird flu and H1N1 influenza outbreaks, multidrug-resistant tuberculosis in New York, the dangers of the anthrax spores mailed to media and politicians in 2001, hantavirus in New Mexico, Ebola in West Africa and in Dallas — the list is so long it would fill pages. So, American politicians, ignore me if you wish, shrug off the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention if you are so inclined, poo-poo the WHO, and turn your back on the Floridian governor if you can — but open your ears when Tony Fauci speaks. On June 6, Fauci warned Francis Collins, the director of the National Institutes of Health, and his advisors that Zika poses a threat unlike any we have previously faced. Research funds were urgently needed, Fauci said, to understand how the once-benign and largely ignored mosquito virus transformed into the greatest threat to pregnant women and their babies since the 1964 rubella epidemic. In the pre-vaccine 1960s, rubella, or German measles, was the primary cause of child blindness, deafness, miscarriage, and other congenital abnormalities in the United States. But Zika is actually worse than rubella because the virus feeds on neural progenitor cells, turning the would-be baby brain cells into Zika virus production factories and eventually burning the cells out. One by one, a nerve cell destined to control hearing, or vision, or memory, or balance, is killed off. The thousands of microcephalic babies born so far in South America and the Caribbean have had so many of their brain cells devoured by voracious viruses that there literally was insufficient mass to, as happens in normal fetal development, push the cranial bone upward to form a nice round skull. But we have only begun to appreciate the range of neurological disorders Zika is inflicting on a generation of babies, because most of the afflicted are still too young to have reached key developmental markers, such as the ability to hold their head upright, capacity to recognize their parents, and the full range of hearing, walking, talking, and learning. Taking a page from cytomegalovirus (CMV), which can also be passed in utero from mother to fetus, only a small percentage suffer microcephaly and obvious deformities, while far larger numbers experience a vast array of learning deficits and brain dysfunctions that only become apparent later in childhood. Many psychiatric disorders that may be overlooked in infancy or early childhood are now known to stem from maternal viral infections damaging fetal brain development, including CMV, Borna disease virus, influenza linked to schizophrenia, herpes simplex virus (type 1) linked to bipolar disorders, and a long list of other fetal infections causing everything from autism- like syndromes to acute depression long after the infected child’s birth. Enough is enough, politicians. Pay heed to Puerto Rico, which, though it is a territory not a state, is inhabited by U.S. citizens. Enough is enough, politicians. Pay heed to Puerto Rico, which, though it is a territory not a state, is inhabited by U.S. citizens. For months, Fauci, the CDC, and Puerto Rican health authorities have warned that a potentially catastrophic Zika epidemic was coming and pleaded for resources to address the crisis. The numbers of infected, symptomatic, and, yes, microcephalic babies were negligible for many weeks. But now, the word “crisis” is literally applicable to the island’s situation, as Zika diagnoses are soaring and the CDC on Friday declared, “The situation in Puerto Rico warrants urgent, comprehensive action to protect pregnant women.” A month ago, Puerto Rico’s mosquito problems and Zika spread seemed manageable — just as Florida’s now appear — but today, despite aggressive mosquito-control efforts and public education campaigns, the population is beset by viral threat, with the number of diagnosed cases (which represent less than 20 percent of actual infections, most of which are asymptomatic) increasing by 1 percent per week. Consider this: A 1 percent increase in the first week of June may seem trivial, but by the first week of August, it is a 9 percent increase, by Labor Day a 14 percent jump, and soon tens of thousands of Puerto Ricans will have been symptomatically infected with Zika, suffering from symptoms and side effects including mild fevers and rashes, paralysis, miscarriage, and giving birth to deformed babies. And this entire explosive spread in Puerto Rico will transpire before Congress returns to Capitol Hill from summer recess. Come on, congressional representatives and senators: This is a pandemic in progress. Reconvene immediately, negotiate a deal, focus on financing, and get the job — your job — done. Failure to do so will mean that every Zika-related birth defect, miscarriage, and paralysis case will be your fault. Photo credit: TIM SLOAN/AFP/Getty Images

Worked with the crew of CBS 60 Minutes (Jon LaPook) who are covering the first patient getting the Phase 1 DNA Zika vaccine (from VRC). We filmed me in the room with the patient (Catherine Paquette). This is part of a special profile that 60 minutes is doing on me. Appeared on Bloomberg TV; Airtalk (NPR – LA) Radio; CNN (Brian Todd for Wolf Blitzer Show 15th case of Zika in the Wynwood section of Dade County, north of Miami

Zika intensity still high. Much press. Did CNN “New Day” with Alisyn Camorata; MSNBC; Diane Rehm Show; AP (Malcolm Ritter); big press telebriefing for the start of the Phase 1 DNA Zika vaccine trial (VRC 319) – followed by countless print media and NPR broadcasts of my Q and A following the press telebriefing; CNN medical online; Texas Community Magazine; WUSF Tampa NPR; Taped for tomorrow’s CBS Morning News.

Article in USA Today with a photo of me. This is a very good picture for the book since it has me in the WH Briefing room with the WH logo at the podium Great article in The Atlantic (August 3, 2016) on the world’s neglet of addressing TB. It is an article that liberally quotes me, Paul Farmer, and Glenda Gray. Battle still going on between Dems and GOP regarding Zika funding. Much press regarding the vaccine trial as well as the funding issue, and the Florida situation: The Morning Drive (A Haitian Radio Show in Miami); BBC radio; PBS Charlie Rose; John Catsimatidis Radio (NYC); New York Times Interview with Catherine St. Louis (Science Times); CBS Evening News. Obama who decided that a whole of government response was necessary since the President was concerned about the honest assessment of Tom that Puerto Rico was a disaster. My first visit to Cuba. Met with various leading members of the medical community (see below) Stayed at the Hotel Nacionale de Cuba – an extraordinary place. It is the hotel that the Hollywood stars and celebrities of the 1940s and 1950s used to stay. It is also the iconic hotel represented by the famous scene in "The Godfather, Part 2" where Michael Corleone played by Al Pacino whispered in his brother Fredo's ear played by John Cazale; "Fredo, you broke my heart", fully intending to ultimately kill his own brother because Fredo betrayed him. It was a New Year's Eve party in the ballroom that I actually saw. It was the night that Fulgencio Batista abruptly left the party to escape from Havana to the Dominican Republic because Fidel Castro was outside of the city. One of the most fun things that I have done in a long time was to drive to and from the hotel and restaurants in old town of Havana in the restored 1950s old cars for which Havana is famous. I only saw Havana, but it was actually very beautiful particularly the extraordinary shoreline that looks out into the Caribbean and the Straits of Florida. It is interesting that most of the people at least outwardly seem in awe of what Castro had accomplished for Cuba, particularly the health care system and the dramatic increase in literacy. I found it interesting that the leading physicians in Cuba have all heard of me and I was somewhat of a hero to them. In particular, several of them mentioned to me that they had read my early papers on vasculitis, they had studied from Harrison's textbook of medicine and they were very familiar with my work on HIV AIDS. It was an unusual time in Cuba since I left for Cuba on a Sunday, and Fidel Castro had suddenly passed away at age 90 on the Saturday before the Sunday that I left. I almost made a wrong decision to cancel the trip. However, the Foreign Ministry of Cuba as well as the US ambassador (Amb De Laurentis) to Cuba insisted that we should go on with the Flavivirus Meeting, which had been co-organized between NIAID and the Cuban Ministry of health, who had visited me already twice over the past year. They felt that given Fidel's intense interest in medicine and science that it would be a show of respect for him if we went ahead with the meeting despite the declared nine days of mourning which actually began when I arrived on Sunday, November 27. The only difference in the atmosphere was that music was not played in the hotel lobby, which is usually a medlay of Latin American music. In addition, there was no music played in any of the restaurants that I went to, even though the atmosphere seemed very normal with many crowds in the restaurants. My impression of the Cuban scientists particularly those at the biotechnology center where Dr. Perez showed me around was that they were very oriented towards the development of products such as diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. In addition, almost everything they did related to peptide research, particularly in the arena of therapeutics. I gave the keynote address at the meeting which took place in the Hotel Nacionale. After that, I spent the two days that I was there visiting everything from individual doctor's offices, to polyclinics, to secondary hospitals, to tertiary hospitals where the most modern medicine was being practiced. I was particularly impressed by visiting the polyclinics which are closely connected with the individual private physicians of patients. Accessibility to the polyclinics for routine medical care actually took place on a 24-hour basis. In other words, if you had a medical or dental problem at any time of the day or night you could go to a polyclinic with there was someone on call 24 hours a day. If your problem was more severe than a routine issue, and ambulance or other form of transportation would take you to the appropriate facility at a higher level. I was told that there were hundreds of polyclinics scattered around Cuba. In this street, hotel, and restaurants, there was a very friendly tone towards Americans. There was an extraordinary amount of tourism seemingly from all over the world, with only a relatively small percentage coming from the United States. President Obama has indicated that he wants to open up interactions and collaborations with the Cubans. We will have to wait and see whether this actually comes to pass under a Trump administration. Fred Hiatt of Washington Post in his usual intellectual manner expressed concern about the Trump antics. However, he feels that the press cannot play into being painted by Trump as “the opposition party”. At the ball saw everyone – Ivanka Trump, etc.

Received very nice e-mail from Denis McDonough sending me his post-

administration contact imformation. See below: From: denis mcdonough @gmail.com] Sent: Sunday, January 29, 2017 9:45 AM To: Fauci, Anthony (NIH/NIAID) [E] Subject: Thanks and contact Tony - What a joy it has been working with you over these years. Thanks for everything, from your great counsel to your endless kindness. Meanwhile, I also want you to have my coordinates going forward. I can be reached on @gmail.com and on cell at . With appreciation and admiration, DM

Over the past several days, Trump (with Bannon as the behind the scenes guru) has been signing a flurry of Executive orders that is putting DC and the press and more than half the country into fits: 1) Repeal ACA; 2) Ban on Muslims entering country from 6 countries (for now) – Iran, Iraq, Sudan, Yemen, Somalia, Libya. He is not calling it a “ban”, but it is; 3) Fired Acting Attorney General who opposed this ban; 4) Freeze on Federal hiring; 5) certain agencies cannot communicate with Congress or the Press, etc. Last night (Jan. 31) he nominated Neil Gorsuch for Supreme Court Justice to replace Scalia. Much opposition. Met with a group of Japanese college and graduate students from the University of Tokyo’s Global Leadership Program for Social design and Management. They were visiting DC and NYC as part of their program. I spoke on how we respsond to emerging and re-emerging IDs. They were absolutely lovely, charming and fun. Almost all young women, many very beautiful. Very enjoyable. Got a nice note today from Bart Haynes regarding a chapter that I wrote for an edition of

Immunological Reviews that he edited. See below his e-mail: From: Barton Haynes, M.D. @duke.edu] Sent: Wednesday, February 01, 2017 8:00 PM To: Fauci, Anthony (NIH/NIAID) [E] Subject: a present Hi tony; Here is a file of all the chapters of the vol. 275 Immunological Reviews on HIV and Abs. Unfortunately IR doesn’t publish a book hardcopy of the journal anymore, so I can’t send you a copy with a message inside – so here is the cyber message with the “book”….. “To Tony: mentor, colleague, friend and father/brother, with gratitude for all you have taught me about science, administration and life, and with great hopes for the future. All the best, Bart” Well I still think its always better as a hard copy….. Bart

Last night, went to Children’s Inn-sponsored Congressionl reception at the Rayburn Building to mingle with old and new members of Congress. Cokie Roberts did her usual Maitresse-de. Debbie Dingle and Sen. Roy Blunt praised me and what I have done for so many years. GOP Congressmen such as Pete Sessions (R-TX) who is becoming a good friend hinted skepticism about the way Trump is rolling things out. Got an interesting call today from Bob Charrow (old friend and former GOP operative from Reagan and George H.W. Bush administration). Bob asked me if I would consider being “acting Director of NIH”. I told him no, but this obviously means that the Trump folks do not want to renew Francis Collins, otherwise why would they be asking me if I wanted to be “Acting”. Bob said that it looks like they do not want to keep Francis on and Larry Tabak is not enough of a “national figure” to serve as acting. This is very similar to the situation of when Zerhouni left and Raynard Kington was deputy and the Bush people did not want him to be Acting and asked me as a well-known national figure (I said no, of course). This whole thing is somewhat troubling since if they do not want Francis, there is a possibility that we may get some weirdo as Director.

Amazing amount of push-back from states (Governors and Attorney Generals) against the immigration/Muslim ban. Many suing the administration. The White House up to now has really been “amateur hour”. They just rushed out with Executive orders without vetting it with the people who know what is going on like the professionals in the State Dept. and DHS and DOJ.

Christine’s 65th birthday! Met with John-Arne Rottingen, interim CEO of CEPI (Coalition for Epidemic preparedness Innovations) in my office. Discussion was on how NIH and CEPI can work together. He actually wanted suggestions (due to my experience) on how he can engage to broader USG to get money for CEPI. Also, without going into specifics, we alluded to smoothing out the rough interactions that we have had in relation to the Ring vaccination study in Guinea for Ebola. Spoke to Cliff today about the meeting and Cliff is adamant that he wants nothing to do with John-Arne, WHO, Marie-Paule Kieny or any of that crew. He is still very angry about the interactions surrounding Ebola. Tonight went to a reception/dinner at CSIS to Discuss CEPI with John-Arne and an interested group of people – Bob Kadlac, George Korsch, Julie Gerberding, many drug company reps, Tom Evans (World Bank), Mark Fineberg (IAVI), etc.

A few weeks ago I sent a get well note to president George H. W. Bush who together with Barbara Bush was admitted to a hospital in Houston with pneumonia following a URI. Today, in a personal note dated February 3, the president sent me a wonderful note of thanks for expressing my wishes for a speedy recovery. What an

amazing man! Below is a PDF of that note:

Gave Keynote Address at the AAAAI Annual Meeting in Atlanta, GA. Even though it was the AAAAI, Tom Fleischman (from NIH) the current President of AAAAI wanted me to speak on any subject, so I gave the talk on “Emerging and Re- emerging Infectious Diseases: A Perpetual Challenge” based on my 32 years advising 5 Presidents on the threats and giving the story of my briefing the Trump Cabinet right before they were officially sworn in. Speaking of Trump, he is acting more and more “crazy”. Today, he tweeted and accused Obama of tapping his personal phone in Trump Towers. The FBI came out and said this was absolutely untrue. Trump said he heard it in the news (Breitbart) and so it must be true. Very weird!!

Amazing Evening! Catherine and Wayne Reynolds asked me at the last minute (yesterday) to attend a dinner of 10-12 people at the residence of the British Ambassador to the USA Sir Kim and Lady (Vanessa) Darroch. The residence is within the compound of the British Embassy of Massachusetts Avenue, NW. The dinner was in honor of Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner. Also present were Supreme Court Justice Anthony Kennedy and his wife Mary, Dina Powell of the White House, Elaine Chao (Secretary of Transportation) and Chris Lidell, Director of Strategic Initiatives at the White House. Delightful evening. Ivanka is elegant, very nice, completely down to earth. Spoke of her children and how much she likes DC. She did not know who I was until Catherine Reynolds explained. Jared, on the other hand, knew exactly who I was and kept thanking me for my service and “great work to keep us safe”. He went on during the dinner conversation to discuss how he thinks that the classic press is dead. Social media is the way to get information. He mentioned that he keeps telling Trump not to worry about what CNN says since they have 1 million viewers and his Twitter account and Face Book reaches 40 million people. The NY Times and CNN are superfluous according to Jared. Also had great conversations with Anthony Kennedy. He really is a good guy. All in all it was a great evening.

Cat Paules’s and my Perspective on Yellow Fever came out yesterday in the NEJM. Good press interest with articles today in Washington Post, L.A. Times, STAT, MedPage and TV interview on WJLA. Also, did radio interview with FOX. Also did a CNN video This evening received the 2017 Lifetime Achievement Award from the Maryland Tech Council given at an elegant affair at the Bolger Center. I received the award together with my friend David Rubenstein (C0-CEO of the Carlyle Group). Very nice things were said about me – standing ovation for me and for David. David was very funny (he has a great sense of humor. He reminded the audience that many years ago, he came to my office at NIH and offered me a job at Carlyle and then said with a straight face that I turned it down and what a shame that I would have contributed so much more as a venture capitalist that in saving millions of lives like I have done since he offered me the job.

Trump acting even more crazy of late. Accusing President Obama of having “wiretapped” trumps phone in Trump Tower duing the campaign. Saying he read about it and it is true. When asked to provide evidence, he had none. Is essence, he was accusing Obama of a criminal act. Then his staff was tasked with explaining this, and they looked like fools on TV and the media, especially Sean Spicer (spokesman) and Kellyanne Connway, who always looks like an idiot. They are a scary bunch.

Learned this evening as the pre-word of the 2018 President’s “Skinny’ (or preliminary ) Budget comes out that Trump will slash government by double digits. Propose to cut State and EPA by around 30 percent. HHS cut is 18 percent with NIH getting 18 percent plus we need to assume cost of ARC as well as assume cost of “21st Century Cures Act” (told you so – I hate authorization without appropriations). This gives us about a 20 percent cut – largest propose cut in history for NIH. Also, he is eliminating the Fogarty International Center!! Hopefully the Congress will block this. Big night tonight! I received the 2017 Research! America legacy Award that they give out 4 times over the past 20 years. Other awardees were Kathy Bates (actress) who received the Isadore Rosenfeld Award for Impact on Public Opinion. She was wonderful with me, praising my work and saying what an honor it was to meet me. Also, Phil Sharp, Lee Hartwell, and Sen. Lamar Alexander received awards. Best part of the night was Joe Biden who received the Gordon and Liura Gund leadership Award. Joe was amazingingly kind to me in his acceptance, calling me out multiple times and telling the audience about the many times he and I and Obama were in the White House together during the Ebola and Zika crises. He stated that I “saved the country and the world from an Ebola outbreak. Great guy!
The scientific community is incredulous about the proposed cuts. Trump and his people are truly unscrupulous. This is outrageous!

Patty Conrad’s last day. She is taking a 3 month detail to help HHS and Secretary Price get their scheduling system up and running. She had done this with Secertary Thompson, which is where I met her. She has been with me for about 9 years. OMB does not want NIH (Francis, me and 3 other IC Directors (Gibbons, Gordon and Volkow) to testify at the scheduled House Appropriations Subcommittee Hearing on March 21 and the Hearing has been postponed until the total budget comes out in May.

Francis Collins told me at our weekly 1-on-1 that Sen. Lamar Alexander spoke with Trump about the NIH Director job and Trump said that he heard that Francis just keeps “funding the same people…” and that Trump is not so sure that he wants Francis. Alexander argued forcibly for Francis. Let us see how this turns out.

Senate Intelligence Committee investigating whether Trump was monitored by the FBI and whether there is any connection between Trump campaign and the Russians. Very partisan arguing going on with Sen. Nunes (GOP chair of committee) clearly trying to ingratitate himself with Trump.

We (NIAID, CDC, FDA, BARDA) are preparing the submission (will brief Sec. Price on April 3) to HHS and OMB of our recource needs to replace the stockpile of H7N9 vaccine that we developed in 2013 with a new H7N9 vaccine since the virus has changed and the stockpile vaccine no longer matches the circulating H7N9, which has changed to another clade that is now highly pathogenic (HPAI) in chickens as opposed to the prior low pathogenic strain (LPAI). Also, many more chicken-to-human cases without sustained human transmission. We (NIAID) are requesting $96 million for 2017-2018. With budget cuts looming, we almost certainly will not get this.

Went to Takeda headquarters in Cambridge, MA with Mike Sneller to discuss our collaboration on Vedolizumab in HIV disease. Gave seminar to the scientific staff of Takeda. Good group with Rajeev Vankayya whom I knew well from the Bush Administration when he was at NSC.

Took quick trip to San Diego to deliver the Opening Keynote for the Annual Meeting of the American College of Physicians (ACP). I spoke on “Emerging and Re-emerging Infectious Diseases” and told the story of my recent briefing of the Trump Cabinet prior to their being sworn in and how I explained that there would certainly be an emerging ID crisis during the Trump administration. 7000 people in the auditorium. I got standing ovation. Great trip!

Next week CNN will air 90 minute documentary called “Unseen Enemy”, which is a story about emerging infectious outbreaks – Ebola, Zika, pandemic flu, smallpox eradication, etc. There is publicity surrounding the buildup to this. I appeared this AM (Sunday) on C-SPAN “Washington Journal” with Janet Tobias, the producer of the film. This evening will be on a panel with Sanjay Gupta as Moderator, Janet Tobias, Nahid Bhadella (Boston U), Peter Sands Chair of International Commission on a Global Health Framework for the Future and Richard Hatchett (new CEO of CEPI). Panel at the National Academy of Medicine (IOM) on 23 and C Street, NW. Nest week I will go the NYC for another panel regarding the film as well as an appearance on CNN (see below).

Briefed HHS Secretary Price on the plans to develop and test vaccine for the re-emerging H7N9 bird flu. Also, Cliff Lane and I received report of the NAM on “Integrating Clinical research into Epidemic Response: The Ebola Experience”. We (NIAID, ASPR, FDA) commissioned the report to tell how we can do better. Great report! They came out strongly defending our stance during the Ebola outbreak that Clinical research is ethical to perform during outbreaks and importantly that RCTs are the optimal way to perform this research in an outbreak setting.

CDC announced that 10% of babies born in the USA to women who had contracted Zika in Southern hemisphere of the Americas had congential abnormalities in brain. I appeared on WTOP Radio to discuss this.
entries.date_note: Source year typo (2016->2017) corrected based on sequence/context.

entries.content: Went to NYC to appear in person with Anderson Cooper, Sanjay Gupta, Janet Tobias and Irwin Redlener on a CNN Panel that will be shown together with the showing of the Documentary “Unseen Enemy”. First time it will air is Friday, April 7, 2017. Will repeat at various future times.
Appeared on the “Situation Room” with Wolf Blitzer talking about the upcoming film “Unseen Enemy” as well as emerging IDs in general.

Was supposed to fly to Detroit to give lecture at University of Michigan (Ann Arbor) for their 200th Anniversary. Went to airport and all planes cancelled due to bad weather in various parts of country that messed up the flight schedules. Weather OK here and in Detroit. Came back to NIH and David Awwad helped to set up my giving the lecture by video. It worked very well. The Panel discussion with Anderson Cooper and Sanjay Gupta aired tonight at 11:45 PM immediately after the showing of “Unseen Enemy”. Looked real good.

Incredibly busy week with multiple talks: CUGH X2, HPTN, VAP, among others. Had dinner on April 12 at the home of Indian Ambassador Sarna on . Amazing home and grounds. Major confrontation with Russia coming up due to our condemning them for helping the Syrian government use sarin gas on their own civilians.

Got a call from Tim Ziemer (formerly the head of the President’s Malaria Initiative (PMI) under president George W. Bush with continuation under Obama. Tim informs me that he has been asked by the Trump people and accepted the position of the Director of Global Health Security and Biodefense at NSC. He wanted to stay connected with me since he knows that when we have an outbreak, I am the ‘go to guy”.

Teleconference with TabAnsari going over a4B7 data in monkeys showing depletion of CD8+ T cells + NK cells + NKT resulted in rebound of viremia. Now need to figure out which of these cell types actually suppressed viremia.

Went to PAHO with Lee Hall to meet with the “Leadership Group (including me)” of the Decade of Vaccines. Also there as part of group – Margaret Chan (WHO), Anthony Lake (UNICEF), Chris Elias (BMGF), Seth Berkley (GAVI). We discussed the gaps in our approach to eliminating vaccine preventable diseases. It was clear that the research agenda part of the effort (i.e. NIAID) was doing the best.

Went to Children’s National Medical Center to deliver a lecture on ZIKA: One Year Later. The people at Children’s had experience with Zika microcephalic and congenital abnormalities babies born in USA from travel-related Zika. Extremely positive reaction to my lecture. See email below from a researcher at

Children’s: From: Kousa, Youssef @childrensnational.org] Sent: Tuesday, April 25, 2017 10:07 PM To: Fauci, Anthony (NIH/NIAID) [E] Subject: Thank You! Dear Dr. Fauci, I hope that you are very well. I just wanted to sincerely thank you for coming to Children's National and giving a remarkable Grand Rounds lecture that we will continue to talk about in the days, weeks and months to come. I also wanted to sincerely thank you for giving me an opportunity to share with you my work on genetic risk factors in Congenital Zika Syndrome. Speaking with you about my project is a highlight in my training as a physician-scientist. Thank you so much once again and I look forward to sharing my results with you in the months and years to come. I am including below my contact information at Children's and NIH below. Best Regards, Youssef -- Youssef A. Kousa, D.O., Ph.D., M.S., (PL-2) Pediatric Residency Program Child Neurology Track Children's National Health System 111 Michigan Avenue, NW Washington, D.C. 20010

Pager: E-Mail: @cnmc.org -- Youssef A. Kousa, D.O., Ph.D., PGY-2 Guest Researcher, Muenke Lab National Human Genome Research Institute National Institutes of Health 35 Convent Drive, Building 35 Bethesda, MD 20892-3717 E-Mail: @nih.gov That night (April 24) I went to CSIS to deliver dinner talk on Malaria in conjunction with the Alan J. Magill Malaria Symposium. Very nice reception to my talk.
Briefed Secretary Price on Pandemic and universal influenza vaccines in the Humphrey Building (610F) conference room. Also briefing were Anne Schuchat, Rick Bright, and George Korsch and Mitch Wolfe.

Went to Fischer’s Lane and gave lecture to Annual Meeting of VTEU’s. Spoke on the situation in DC with Trump Budget, etc. Gave them taste of reality of what the future will bring. Went downtown to GW to lecture to the Elizabeth Glazer Pediatric AIDS Foundation – Spoke on Ending the AIDS Pandemic and remaining scientific challenges. Extremely well-received with standing ovation. Invited by CEO Chip Lyons. Ran into old friends such as Jen Cohen, formerly of MSF. One Ugandan Country Lead said at the end of lecture that he learned more in the 40 minutes of my lecture than he has in 10 years of lectures on AIDS.

Went to the 2017 Annual Garden Brunch before the White House Correspondent’s Ball at Connie Milstein’s home ) hosted by Tammy Haddad, Kevin Sheekey, Hilary Rosen, Constance Milstein, Mark & Sally Ein, Fred Humphries, Kelley McCormick and Franco Nuschese. Usual fun cast of characters. Had nice conversation with Don Lemon of CNN. He praised my work; I told him how much I admired his courage in pushing back on his show the crazy “alternate truth” statement of Trump supporters like Jeffrey Lord. He was very moved by my appreciation of what he is doing. Also ran into Ian Kahn who plays George Washington on TV. Spoke with his last year and today. He told me that my conversation with him last year inspired him to use his role to try and make a differenc in pushing for responsibility and bipartisanship. Also, spoke with Leslie Dach (former chief-of-staff to Sylvia Burwell); Bob Bennett (DC Lawyer); Hilary Rosen; Neera Tanden; Greta vanSusteren; among others. Mostly a Democratic group bemoaning the craziness of the Trump administration. President Trump did not attend the Ball (I was not invited this year). Went to Children’s Inn Gala tonight at the Ritz Carlton Tyson’s Corner.

Went to premier first “partial” screening of the Discovery Channel 3 part production of “First in Human” documentary on the NIH Clinical Center held at the Auditorium of the Ronald Reagan Building at 1300 Pensylvania Ave, NW. Followed by panel chaired by Jon LaPook from CBS (my old friend). Chris and I and Jon went out for a beer at the Willard Hotel across the street afterwards. Jon is concerned and going to cover what looks like an outbreak of Zika in Brownsville, TX. Interesting budget battles for NIH. The House and Senate (led by Tom Cole and Roy Blount, respectively) proposed an omnibus bill for a $2 billion increase for NIH for 2017.

Visit to NIH of King Gustav of Sweden. I presented our work on Antibiotic resistance. The King and the Swedish health authorities are very interested in the problem of AMR. That evening Chris and I had amazing dinner (invited by Catherine and Wayne Reynolds) at the Jefferson Hotel. Present at the dinner: Secretary of State Rex Tillerson, Senate Leader Mitch McConnell, Transportation Secretary Elaine Choi, Viet Nam war hero General Jack Keane, Rick and Jane Atkinson, Justice Anthony Kennedy and wife Mary, Steve and Alice Rosenberg, Brendon and Mrs. Sullivan among others. Rex Tillerson was quite open and transparent about the problems with North Korea and China. He feels that we need to engage Kim Jong Un and convince him that we are not a threat to him. China does not want to engage in hostilities. They realize that if they lose soldiers in the context of the 1 child rule, then that family heritage stops. They do not want war despite their building up of a military. Also, China President Xi Jinping told him that when China engaged against us during the Korean War, it set back the one China effort 100 years. If they engaged us now, it would destroy their economic growth. They do not want war. And so he feels that if we do not try to embarrass them or interfere in their internal issues, that they will control Korea’s antics. Also, I gave to the group under Catherine’s request an update on Zika, particularly Zika vaccine. Mitch McConnell was quite complimentary to me about this. Also, learned that my dear friend Bob Curran died . I will go up to providence (Rumford), RI for his funeral on Monday, May 8.

Went to Rumford, RI for the funeral mass, burial (he was cremated and his ashes buried in the cemetery, and then to the reception at the Brwn University faculty Club. I am so glad that I went up for the event. Bob’s wife Peg and his children Robert E. Curren III, Trevor and Victoria were thrilled to see me. I was surprised to hear from people such as his ophthalmology nurses from his office that he “spoke about you all the time saying how you were his mentor and his very best friend forever”. People I met who were his neighbors for the past 40+ years since he came back to Massachusetts/RI kept saying how Bob always used to talk about me and the great times we had together including our famous summer together touring Europe in our Deux Chaveau (French mini-car). I had major flashbacks there and on the trip home about the truly amazing times that Bob and I had together. We first met when I played against him in basketball in the St. Agnes of Rockville Center Tournament when we were 16 and 17 years old. We then were inseperable through college, medical school, internship/residency and then NIH. He got married at end of residency and so after that he was more of a family man during the years at NIH. Truly a great man and a dear, dear friend.

Briefed Sec. Price in Conference Room 610F of the Humphrey Building on Antibiotic Resistance. Together with CDC, FDA, BARDA, CMS, HRSA, etc. preparing the Secertary for his trip to the World Health Assembly in Geneva. He is a very reserved man with a sense of humor. Tonight, I drove in a rainshower from NIH to Baltimore for Bob Gallo’s 80th Birthday Party at the Grand Hotel on North Charles Street. I gave one of the laudatios. At my Table with Bob and MaryJane and also giving laudatios for Bob were: former Governors Parris Glendening and Martin O’Malley; Kathleen Kennedy Townsend. Hard to believe that Bob is 80 years old. Had conversation with O’Malley about his Presidential run. He is as shocked as everyone about Trump. He said he never had a chance against Hillary since she had her machince, which actually messed up completely in the general election.

(Monday) – Did a 2 hour tape for a CBS special on HIV/AIDS – an historical look to air on CBS Sunday Show. The shoot was run by Rita Braver (Bob Barnett’s wife). Bright, sunny crisp, clear day, around 70 degrees F. Went to West Wing of White House (6:00 PM) to meet with Reed Cordish (Assistant to the President) in preparation for a planned meeting the following day with President Trump on a multitude of issues: the usual vaccine/autism story; restriction in # of grants per investigator; Bayh-Dole Act; economic impact of NIH research. The meeting was mostly for Francis, but Francis wanted me along for my “gravitas” and my experience with vaccines. Also, Larry Tabak was there. Reed had agreed to have all of us meet with the President tomorrow, but the agenda was packed for a 30 minute planned meeting in the Oval Office. I cancelled 2 lectures for tomorrow to be at the WH. At the pre-brief meeting today were: Chris Liddell (Assistant to the POTUS, whom I met at the dinner at the British Ambassador’s house several weeks ago – really good guy- New Zealander); Mary-Sumpter Lapinsky (HHS); Katy Talento (Domestic Policy Coouncil). Towards the end of meeting, Reed mentioned that the agenda for tomorrow’s meeting would have to ultimately be approved by Ivanka Trump who had just left for a dinner. Also, the # of people at the meeting tomorrow would have to be approved by her. As it turned out, after we left the WH and I go home, Larry and Francis e-mailed me and forwarded an e-mail from Reed saying that Ivanka changed the agenda to 1 tiem – the NIH budget for 2018 and she wanted a small meeting with just Francis and Secretary Price. Thus, Larry and I are “scratched”. Too bad I cancelled the lectures. However, I got to meet Reed and Chris (again) and Katy. Also, I know now who actually runs the White House agenda – Ivanka.

Testified at the House Appropriations Subcommitteee Hearing at 10:00 AM. Chair: Tom Cole (R-OK). Despite the Trump budget asking for >20% cut in the NIH budget, it was a love fest for NIH with everyone (GOP and Dems) saying that they will actually increase the NIH budget as they had just done with the Omnibus Bill for FY 2017 in which they increased the NIH budget by $2 Billion over FY2016. I had the opportunity to “eloquently” (as said by many) defend the Fogarty International Cwenter (FIC) that the Trump Budget statement abolished.

Testified before the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on oversight and Investigations on Zika. Chaired by Tim Murphy (R-PA). Hearing went very well. Many questions aimed at me regarding progress on the Zika vaccine. Overall, very friendly. I bailed out Lyle Peterson (CDC) a few times when he was in trouble. He was very thankful.

Tonight I receive e-mail from:

Susanna Visser, DrPH, MS Associate Director for Policy Division of Vector-Borne Diseases National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases Centers for Disease Control and Prevention She thanked me for being so supportive of CDC. Very nice e-mail. Also, Tom Frieden e- mail me saying that he was thinking of me and missed our relationship. He hinted that he has accepted his “dream job” but could not give details at this point. More later.

Presented my “State of NIAID” talk to the Annual HVTN meeting at the Omni Shoreham Hotel in DC. Spoke about the Trump budget (-26% for NIH) as well as the expanded Mexico City Policy and other items of interest.
Low level press continues on a variety of issues. Today did Swedish Public Radio on progress in Zika vaccines.

Very interesting and somewhat disturbing day. Met with Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. together with Francis Collins, Larry Tabak, Josh Gordon, Diana Bianchi, Linda Birnbaum and people from RFK, Jr’s inner circle. RFK, Jr asked for the meeting (in medical Board Room – 4th Floor Clinical Center) to talk about the danger of vaccines including, but not limited to thimerasol and autism. Sadly, he went on for over 1 hour stating points that were clearly inaccurate. One example – he listed a whole bunch of diseases of various organ systems and said that these diseases were definitely caused by vaccines. It was a very painful 2 hours spent with him. He distorts the literature and denies anything that argues against him Reed Cordish from the White House was at the meeting. The meeting occurred since Jared Kushner wanted us to meet with RFK, Jr. in order to report back to President Trump who seems enamoured of RFK, Jr. Cordish got the point about how off base RFK, Jr is. RFK, Jr has serious spastic dysphonia and it was difficult to understand him, which was complicated by the emotional effort that he put into his presentation. I actually felt very sorry for him since he clearly means well, but is completely incorrect in his information. After it was over, I went back to him as he was leaving Building 10 and told him that although I explicitly said in the meeting that I totally disagree with most of what he said and I believe that he is fundamentally incorrect in his statements and conclusions, nonetheless, I admire and respect him for his passion in trying to protect children from harm. He was very moved and told me that coming from me, this meant a lot to him. We shall see where this goes vis-à-vis the POTUS.

Spent the better part of today with Bill Gates who made his yearly visit to NIH. I was on a panel with him in the Porter Building, I introduced another panel and importantly, I took 1hour and showed him around the VRC. He has always been very interested in my viewpoints on areas of common interest with the BMGF. He has recently announced the creation of Medical Research Institue (MRI) centered in Boston and Seattle ($100 million) to pursue research and importantly translational development in TB, Malaria, and enteric diseases. He hopes to collaborate with me and NIAID in these endeavors.
Had major appearance in a CBS Special for Sunday AM on “CBS Sunday Morning” . Subject was 36 years of HIV/AIDS. Rita Braver (Bob Barnett’s wife) was the producer.

Beautiful 70 degree dry Monday in DC. Most of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee members and their staff visited NIH today for several hours. I hosted a 35 minute tour (with a introductory talk by me on the history of the VRC with John Mascola. Visiting us were: Sens. (Chairman) Roy Blunt (R-MO), Patty Murray (D-WA), Richard Durbin (D-IL), Lamar Alexander (R-TN), James Lankford (R- OK), John Kennedy (R-LA) Jean Shaheen (D-NH), Susan Collins (R-ME). Great visit. This evening went to George Washington Medical School (Ross Hall – Room 117) to participate (gave a laudatio) in the ceremony conferring the Murdock Head Chair Professorship of Medicine and Health Policy on Bopper Deyton.

Gave my annoual “career inspiration” talk to the IDSA Fellows, this time at the Pooks Hill Marriott. Spoke about my briefing the soon-to-be Trump Cabinet on the danger of emerging microbes and worked into this the importance of the discipline of ID.

Went to Holy Cross for my 55th year Reunion!!! Yikes! I was the featured speaker for the Class, which was an interview of me on stage by my old friend Pete Deckers. Also, took many questions from the audience of my classmates and their wives. They much appreciated my presence. I missed the fact that Bob Curran was not there having died just a few weeks ago.

Visited my cousin Reynard Milici in Haydensville, MA and spent a lot of time with him showing Chris and me his studio with so many of his magnificent paintings. He is truly a great artist. That evening went to the home of Jamie Gorelick and Rich Waldron for their Annual Spring Garden Party. Much conversation about the “craziness” of Trump, particularly around the testimony of James Comey before the Senate Intelligence Committee this past week. Had conversations with Jamie (who is the laywer of Jared Kushner re: his “conflict of interest”, David Ignatius (Post), Fred Hiatt (Post), Ruth Marcus (Post), E.J. Dionne (Post). All agreed that if Trump went under oath the way he is threatening to do to contradict Comey, he would likely lie under oath.
Gave tour of VRC to various members of media, Mostly modern blogs like “STAT”, etc.

Went to Boston to participate in the The Atlantic PULSE: “On the Front Lines of Health Care”. Done in collaboration with STAT. Moderator of my panel which I did with Vanessa Kerry was Jeffrey Goldberg (Editor of the Atlantic). We discussed panemic preparedness. After the panel, I did a “Facebook Live” interview with Jeff.

The Rachel Maddow Show / The MaddowBlog The Great 2014 Sunday Show Race 12/29/14 12:30 PM—Updated 12/29/14 02:14 PM By Steve Benen A year ago, House Intelligence Committee Chairman Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) made more Sunday show appearances than anyone else in the country. This year, Rogers’ dominance was even more pronounced, though that’s only part of the larger story. Just like last year, I tallied up the guests for “Meet the Press,” “Face the Nation,” “This Week,” “State of the Union,” and “Fox News Sunday,” and once again, Republican voices easily outnumbered their Democratic counterparts. In fact, this year was even more one-sided in the GOP’s favor.

The above chart shows every political figure who made 10 or more Sunday show appearances this year – based on Nexis transcripts and the shows’ archives – with red columns representing Republicans, blue columns representing Democrats, and purple columns representing those who aren’t part of either party. Rogers easily outpaced the field last year with 27 appearances, and this year, he did even better, making 30 appearances. To put that in perspective, that works out to an average of roughly one appearance every 1.7 weeks (or 2.5 Sunday show appearances a month, every month for a year).

House Homeland Security Committee Chairman Mike McCaul (R-Texas) was the only other person to reach 20 appearances this year, though he still ended up trailing Rogers by a large margin. Sen. John McCain (R-Ariz.), a Sunday-show staple for a generation, was third with 15, tied with Dr. Anthony Fauci, the non-partisan head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, who made a flurry of media appearances to discuss the Ebola threat in the fall.

But further down the rankings, some interesting numbers pop up.

For example, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was one of the more popular guests this year, to the point that he made more appearances than any Democratic official in Congress or in the Obama administration. In fact, 15 people made 10 or more appearances on Sunday shows this year, and only three Democrats made the cut – and they’re all at the bottom of the list.

Of the 15 most frequent guests, 14 are men. All 15 are white.

I should note that for the purposes of this study, I excluded hosts and journalists, looking exclusively at current officials, former officials, candidates for public office, domestic or foreign policymakers, or anyone fairly characterized as actively involved in the political arena. (Karl Rove’s inclusion here is admittedly debatable, but given his role in the Crossroads operation, it seemed only fair to characterize him as someone who’s “in the arena.” He has a media role, to be sure, but Rove also hopes to directly influence the outcome of the elections on which he comments.)

There is a school of thought, articulated by the estimable Jonathan Bernstein among others, that says tallies like these are unimportant – whether Sunday shows prefer Republicans to Democrats is inconsequential, the argument goes, and hardly worth considering in any detail.

Obviously, I disagree. For me, the five major Sunday shows represent a political institution of sorts, highlighting the kinds of voices and ideas the Beltway media considers important. The discussions held on these programs help reflect – and in many cases, shape – the conventional wisdom for the political establishment in D.C.

And a little too often, these discussions suggest to the public that it’s Republicans whose views drive the conversations that matter.

Like last year, I’ll leave it to others to speculate as to why the Sunday shows seem so preoccupied with Republican guests, but I will note that msnbc offers fine programming on weekends, including Sunday mornings, featuring a diverse group of stories and guests unseen elsewhere. (Columbus Day) – note article below that appeared today in the Boston Globe Opinion | Roland Merullo Christopher Columbus and Italian- Americans: a sad marriage David L. Ryan/Globe Staff/File A statue of Christopher Columbus stood in the North End at a park named for the explorer. By Roland Merullo October 09, 2017 When I was a boy, my father owned a book called “Columbus WAS First.” I never read it. I’m not sure he ever read it, either. But, judging by the title, I can guess what it argued, and I can guess why he kept it on the shelf. Few, if any, modern historians dispute Christopher Columbus’s record of brutality or his pivotal role in the heinous practice of owning and selling human beings. Torture, punitive amputation, wholesale slaughter of the generally peaceful native peoples he encountered on his four voyages — none of that was rare among European explorers of his era. Columbus’s enthusiasm for it, though, while not putting him in a class by himself, certainly calls into question why we continue to celebrate a national holiday in his name. What’s painful to me, and I’m certain would have been painful to my father were he still alive, is that the holiday named for Columbus — chosen to mark the October day on which he first saw land he believed was the Far East — has become the one day each year on which the contributions of Italian-Americans are recognized. It’s a sad marriage. There’s so much to be proud of in the courage, resilience, and achievements of Americans who trace their heritage to the Italian peninsula — and so much to be ashamed of in the nation’s continued elevation of Columbus to hero’s status. As this summer’s events in Charlottesville, Va., underscored, America has a lot to reckon with in terms of its history. Our land is littered with tributes to slave owners and other torturers, to the architects of genocide; some of our universities and libraries are named after people who made their fortunes by poisoning others, or from the sweat and blood of others. Their victims were people of color, yes, particularly and horribly, but also wave after wave of immigrants who happened to arrive a century or three later than the First Exploiters. While it’s clear that our moral consciousness has evolved — behavior once endorsed by queens and bishops, presidents and popes, has become obviously evil in the eyes of the vast majority of Americans — we retain a tendency toward blind hero-worship. Athletes, politicians, CEOs, and celebrities of all stripes are admired for their successes while we often ignore their gross mistreatment of others, and of the earth. Speaking as one Italian-American, I’ll have no problem when statues to Columbus are removed from the public eye. And I won’t mind at all if the second Monday in October is no longer a holiday that bears his name. It will bother me, though, if the grit, talent, and generosity of millions of Italian-Americans is no longer recognized. I could mention Enrico Fermi and Dr. Anthony Fauci, Mercury astronaut Walter Schirra, DiMaggio, Sinatra, De Niro, Madonna, and Lady Gaga, but I’d rather honor the nameless ones who kept house and raised kids, who toiled in shoe and textile factories and carved stone and worked the mines in Appalachia. Italian-Americans endured mockery and exclusion, then watched their culture — so rich in the arts, sciences, and human warmth — reduced to mob stereotypes and Jersey Shore goons. We deserve a special day.
