Invited by Tammy Haddad, Anita McBride, and Connie Milstein to go to a book signing/reception at the Jefferson Hotel (owned by Connie) regarding a book by Greta vonSusteren called “Everything You Need to Know About Social Media”. Great party. Met Senator John McCain’s 106 year old mother and his brother who is an MD. Senator not there. Also, saw and chatted with Anita McBride, Bob Barnett, Hilary Rosen, Kellyanne Conway (invited her to NIH – she has 3 children at StoneRidge). Also, Karen Tumulty (Washingon Post) wants to come to NIH to interview me in the context of her writing a book about Nancy Reagan. I told Anita how much I enjoyed “Sisters First” book by the Bush daughters Jenna and Barbara. She suggested that I write to President Bush to tell him that, which I did. I also e-mailed Jenna and Barbara to congratulate them on the book. They both wrote back with nice e-mails, excited that I had read and liked their book.

Had dinner over Francis Collins’s house to welcome new Surgeon General Jerome Adams. Good guy; young, sincere, a bit naïve, but very smart. Good pick! Also at dinner was Freeman Hrabowski (President, University of Maryland, Baltimore County), Larry Tabak, Roger Glass. Good discussions, but in a not really obnoxious way (but clearly noticeable), Freeman dominated most of the conversation. Having said that, he is really a good guy. I had a bad that night, but soldiered on.

Had dinner over the home of the South African Ambassador to the USA. Home on Rockwood Parkway. Hosted by an NGO and Debbie Birx, Attended by several African Amssadors to the USA – Malawi, Mozambique, Uganda, Namibia, etc. Dinner in anticipation of World AIDS day commemoration tomorrow at State Department.

2 events: 1) Went to State Department for a World AIDS Day Commemoration. Part of panel with audience questions together with Debbie Birx, Tim Zeimer, Garrett Grigsby (HHS-OGA), others. 2) Part of panel at the National Museum of Natural History that showed the documentary film “How to Survive a Plague”. Peter Staley can down for the panel and went out to dinner with him after the panel. Late night. Great to see Peter. Paper that Cat Paules, Kanta Subbarao and I wrote came out Online in the NEJM on “Chasing Season Influenza: The need for a Universal Influenza Vaccine” (see PDF). It was totally honest and described the egg-adapted mutation that led to an “accidental” mismatch in the H3N2 circulating virus and the vaccine. It referenced a recent paper in PNAS by Scott Hensley (NIAID grantee) showing that this is what happened with the Australia vaccine and our vaccine, which was the same. Australia had only a 10% efficacy against H3N2 in their past season and so we warned that since we generally follow Australia that we might have a bad year. Of course the CDC and BARDA got miffed, but what else is new. In any event over the next several days, it got much press, mostly print and national and local NPR and other radio. Went on WTOP to discuss my paper on flu.

Went to the Situation Room of the White House to brief NSC Tom Bossert about the H7N9 influenza threat. Arranged by Lu Borio who is now down at NSC. Tom Bossert is a really good person anad very smart. Tim Zeimer was at the briefing and there was discussion about how we would handle an H7N9 outbreak under various scenarios. Anne Schuchat was there and in typical CDC fashion, she stretched her 10 minutes into 30 minutes. What else is new. Tom and Tim re-enforced that if there is an outbreak, they want me and Anne out there dealing with the messaging.

Went to the (now) annual Holiday party at the home of Norah O’Donnell and Geoff Tracy on . Heavy with media people and A-list folks. Had good conversations with Norah about the Charlie Rose issue and with Jake Tapper about the Trump fiasco. Judy Woodruff, Al Hunt, Mary Hager (producer for “Face the Nation”, etc. Really an enjoyable night.
Pretty sick with what started as a typical

Appeared with Debbie Birx on a panel sponsored by The Washington Post in their downtown building interviewed by Post reporter Lennie Bernstein. Others interviewed on sequential panels were Dionne Warwick, Phill Wilson, Mike Saag. Dionne wanted a picture with me since I have helped her . Lovely woman. Attended in the evening the U.S. Global Leadership Coalition Awards Gala at the Marquis Marriott Hotel in DC. Invited by the ONE organization (Tom Hart). Nikki Haley got the big award and gave a great speech about of responsibility for leadership in global aid and assistance (seems contrary to what Trump has been saying). Senator Lindsey Graham gave a great speech with a similar sentiment. He sounded very presidential. He honored 200 generals who belong to the coalition. They were represented by Gen. Anthony Zinni and Admiral James Stavridis.

Did NPR interview with Rob Stein – will air in next couple of days. Much press interest in the flu article. H3N2 is starting to accelerate in the USA, mostly in southerne state (widespread) but “regional” in several and local in others including Maryland.

Met with Jennifer Ashton, the new Chief medical Correspondent for ABC replacing Rich Besser. With her is Dan Child - ?producer. It was a 1 hour “courtesy” visit to get to know me and start a press relationship. Very good vibes between us (both Jennifer and Dan). Look forward to working with them. alays overpromise to fix the flu problem. Mike Burgess reminded him that this was what Tom Frieden, not I, said a few years ago. Gave briefing call to Nida Najar from Fareed Zakaria/GPS Show at CNN – Flu

Another gala event at the Academy of Achievement given by Wayne and Catherine Reynolds. Am very fortunate that they have befriended Chris and me. Usual incredible cast of A List characters. The function was to honor Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and his wife Susan. Elegant dinner. Had nice conversation with Brent Kavanaugh. Spoke about his and my high school basketball careers in a Jesuit High School. He went Gonzaga here in DC. He, like I, was Captain of his team. Also spoke with Secretary Pompeo about basketball. To my surprise, both Kavanaugh and Pompeo knew very well who I am and what I do. Both were very complimentary. Other folds whom I have gotten to know were there: General James Jones, Chris Wallace, Wolf Blitzer, Rick Atkinson, Robert Langer, Brendan Sullivan, Steve and Jean Case, etc. Also, there was Kellyanne Conway among others. Surprising entertainment at the end of the evening was the amazing Diana Ross. She brought the house down. Great evening!
CNBC again on flu

Media interest continues regarding the “bad” flu season that we are experiencing. Today did NPR (WAMU) together with Mike Osterholm, John Barry, and Elizabeth Rosenthal (Kaiser now; formerly N.Y Times). Later in the Day did WTOP radio. Also, gave interview with Buzzfeed

Flu season expoding. Following similar track (regarding numbers of cases) to 2014-2015 and 2012-2013. However, severity seems worse with stock outs of Tamiflu in California that is very hard-hit. Also tents being put up in different states to handle cases. Much press interest overlapping with the threat of government closure in 4 days due to disagreement between Dems and GOP about budget, CHIP, and DACA. I appear on CNN blog and on an interview for a future 60 minutes Australia TV shot.

Did some podcasts (Paul Vogelzang) on flu. Also NPR NewsHour ONLINE for topical microbicide controversy (merging [eliminating] the microbicide network with HPTN) Did long filmed interview with Smithsonian on Maurice Hilleman; however, it turned into a feature on me to be shown on Smithsonian Website and at the Smithsonian.

News dominated by the raging flu and the threat of government closure. Great appearance on Facebook Live for AP interviewed by Julie Pace (White House Correspondent and Bureau Chief for AP together with Lauren Neergaard on flu. However, also asked me about impact of government closure. It was picked up by all print outlets and TV and went viral. Also did Marc Siegal long radio interview for NYC – “Doctor Radio”

Tension and media interest continue on flu and shutdown. Did VOX interview and NPR Science Friday and TV – i24 NEWS from NYC and TelAviv – all on flu with questions about impact of shutdown. Government shuts down at 11:59 PM on Jan. 19
On 1st anniversary of Trump Presidency, the government shuts down.

Government still shut down (Sunday) The hangup is that the Dems want to put the DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals) resolution into the CR spending bill, but the GOP does not. They want to pass the CR and then when the gov. is open they will consider DACA. The Dems do not trust the GOP since they keep kicking the DACA can down the road. The Dems have offered to put “the Wall” into the bill in exchange for DACA. Steve Miller of the White House (total asshole) says no and so the gov. stays shut. Did FOX News this afternoon about flu.

Was scheduled to do multiple NPRs including “On Point” today (Monday) but HHS is not allowing anyinterviewers while the gov. is closed. Shutdown ends tonight. Resume interest in flu. Dems cave in. They are losing the PR battle. Trump people are calling it the “Schumer Shutdown” and it is sticking. Government re-opens without DACA with promise by Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell that he will take up DACA before the new CR runs out on Feb. 8. I think the Dems are in real trouble since the House is no going to accept a DACA deal nor is the POTUS even if the Senate does. We are likely in for another shutdown. Gave interview to Emily Bass who is writing a history of PEPFAR book

Interesting that unlike prior administrations, HHS is not giving me crap that Flu is CDC turf, and is approving everything we send down. Did LA Times interview. My Perspective on “PEPFAR – 15 years and Counting Lives Saved” came out today in the NEJM, celebrating the 15th anniversary of PEPFAR. Yikes, time flies.

Did WTOP radio today on flu. Still a very bad season.

Also did NPR – WOSU – Ohio – Ann Fisher

Flu continues to rage. Much press interest; however, press interest is also diverted to Trump where evidence that he colluded with the Russians in influencing the election or that he enacted “obstruction of justice” in trying to coerce and manipulate the FBI (fire Comey; threaten to fire Moeller). Trump in Davos Did C-SPAN Washington Journal with Gretta Brawner Also CBS radio – all on Influenza; many blog and print also

Media still hot for flu. Did CBS This Morning with Norah O’Donnell and John Dickerson. Also did NBC Nightly News Trump gives his 1st SOTU address tonight. It was a slight attempt at bi-partisanship, but then eroded into the usual.
Flu stuff hot and heavy. Doing mostly print stuff with Wall Street Journal and Politico

CDC came out with their weekly FluView and the numbers show that this likely will turn out to be the most serious seasonal flu outbreak that we have had since tracking/recording started in 2005. The curve is still going up and so it has surpassed 2014-2015. Did Al Jazeera TV and will do CNN tomorrow (Feb. 3) and Face the Nation on Sunday (Feb. 4)

Did CNN with Fredricka Whitfield on influenza outbreak. Good interview, but heard tonight that Face the Nation is cancelling my segment scheduled for tomorrow (Sunday) due to the commotion about the release today of the Democratic version of the GOP memo attacking the FBI and the DoJ

Did really enjoyable 1 hour televised blog for CBS with Major Garrett at the Tastee Diner in Bethesda on flu + other issues such as PEPFAR. Briefed Secertary Azar on flu down at Conference Room 610F in the Humphrey Building.

Did a Panel on outbreak preparedness with The Economist at the City Club in DC Did interview at the Newseum with Soledad O’Brien for her TV show “Matter of Fact”. Did extended interview with CNBC on Flu here in my office.

CDC flu numbers came out. Cases still increasing. Clearly, this is the worst flu season that we have had since the numbers were recorded (excluding the 2009 pandemic) Did WMAL radio on flu today. Also Worcester Channel 3 TV interview by phone.

Extraordinary visit to lecture at the Ocean Reef Club in Key Largo, FL. Lectured at the Cultural Center on EIDs (the 5 presidents talk). Went with Chris and the 2 ½ days were magical, Beautiful weather, Amazing fishing in “the flats” of the mangrove islands. Unbelievable wealth of the members of the “Club”. Memorable time.
Latest numbers from CDC show that the ILIs seem to have plateaued from last week. Let us see if the trend in now down.

Did a teleconferenced class for the Yale School of Management. It consisted of the Professor interviewing me with questions, followed by questions from the class. Intense interest in flu still present, but somewhat slowing.

Did taping for am upcoming Good Morning America segment on universal flu and flu challenge studies. I was interviewed in the SCSU at the Clinical Center. Did interview with Reuters Also, went to to do a taped interview for the Spanish Language TV show Efecto Naim Also did a podcast on influenza

Did an interview with Fox News (Bret Baier) to be aired tomorrow Crazy request from Francis Collins/Larry Tabak. I have been pushing for new money for Universal Flu Vaccine. We just did a strategic plan. Francis/Larry met with Secretary Azar this afternoon and told him about my plan. Alex likes it and wants us to put together by tomorrow morning (it is now 7:30 PM) a justification for more money (millions) to spend in FY 2018. I am here with Tara trying to contact people to help put together this proposal. Everyone else is gone and Francis needs it by 10:00 AM tomorrow.

Things starting to heat up in a good way regarding attention to and interest in funding our Universal Influenza Vaccine (UIV) efforts. Our strategic plan came out today int the JID. Several radio interviews and print stories about the plan. Went down to OSTP and met with J.P. Cretien and Sara Brenner to discuss our plan for UIV. Also, while at the White House, ran into Tom Gossert who was very interested in helping us get funding. Tom is a great guy and this is interesting since he is White House and this would be busting the budget. Also, House Energy and Commerce Committee want me to come up with a plan for funding UIV from omnibus 2018 through several years after. I submitted through Building 1 a $1 billion plan over 5 to 6 years. E and C committee does not want HHS to know what we have done. Interesting intrigue. Word is that E and C wants to “own” UIV. Everybody wants to be somebody. Definitely seeing the fruits of my emphasizing UIV in medical literature, lay media, talks, etc.
Appeared on taped segment of CBS Evening News with Jon LaPook. It was the segment that we taped as interview + visit to the VRC discussing universal influenza vaccine.
Still considerable press re; H3N2 flu. Mostly print media attention. Today I taped a segment to appear on the Australian version of “60 Minutes”
NY Post interview. Importantly, the flu is now dropping considerably as the curve shoots down. Nonetheless, 119 pediatric deaths thus far and >80 hospitalizations per 100,000 population.

Had my 4year review as NIAID Director. Reviewed by Jim LeDuc, Mark Dybul, Diane Griffin and Ray Dolin. Went very well. Also, Stewart Simonson who is now the Assistant Director-General for Management at WHO came to visit with some WHO colleagues to show them around NIH. I met with them: Ambassador Michèle Boccoz, (ADG for External Relations), and Ranieri Guerra (ADG for Special Initiatives). Had dinner at my home with Stewart 2 nights ago on Sunday, March 4.

Testified before the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations chaired by Gregg Harper (R-NH). Other witnesses: Scott Gottlieb (FDA), Rick Bright (BARDA), Anne Schuchat (CDC). Hearing on influenza response. I spoke on the need for a Universal Influenza Vaccine. Hearing went very well. Chairman and Congressman Walden (Full Committee Chair) particularly liked my graphic slides. Also, I brought in a prop – a 10 million blow-up of a nano-particle with HA stems attached.

(Sunday) – Part of panel hosted by NBC Doreen Gentzler at DC Conventional Center on NIH/Science/Health. It was an NBC4 Health & Fitness EXPO (25th Anniversary). My co-panelist was Teri Manolio (NHGRI). Good session with audience questions. One man (nice fellow) got up and said his wife has a crush on me because I am a “rock star”. He then went on to ask some good questions. Am finished with my book up to end of Obama years and am now editing from beginning to end before I speak with and give it to Rick Atkinson.

Continued unrest and controversy in the Trump administration regarding sex scandal with porn star Stormy Daniels and now ex-Playboy Bunny Karen McDougal. Trump fires Deputy FBI Director McCabe; also fires Secretary of State Rex Tillerson and National Security Advisor. H.R. McMaster. Continued concern that he will fire independent Counsel Robert Mueller. Flu dying down. This has been the WORST flu season for seasonal flu in past decade and probably worst among “seasonal” flus on record. Continued press interest – blogs, some TV and radio on Flu and other ID issues.

Jim Kim (Wold Bank) visits NIH and we discuss future ways that World Bank and NIH can work together to utilize the research discoveries of NIH to synergize with the implementation and “outcomes” mandate of the World Bank. I will be working with Tim Evans to pursue this. Went to the end part of a dinner at the Riggs Library at Georgetown organized by John Monahan to discuss “Pandemic Preparedness”. Seems that everyone (multiple groups – CEPI, NAM, Wellcome) is trying to put together a program in this area.

I am on the Lancet Commission to help towards reaching the WHO End TB goal of 90% reduction in TB ((i.e. end TB) by 2035. Eric Goosby is the Chair of this Commission. They are in New Delhi, India now at a meeting. I could not attend (too much travel and time away) but I am in close touch with Eric and am helping out with the final report of the commission.

Alex Azar visits NIH and in his Town Hall in Masur Auditorium calls me out several times. I have been talking up my support for Alex at NIH. He receives very warm welcome despite the NIH antipathy towards Trump. Garret Grigsby of HHS OGA wants to develop for Alex an HHS-Wide proposal to help with the End TB effort by 2035. I have taken charge of putting together a proposal involving NIH, CDC, and FDA. We have conference call today – Rebecca Martin et al from CDC; Marion Gruber, Ed Cox, et al from FDA; Bob Eisinger in the lead with me for NIH.

HHS announces that Bob Redfield will be the Director of CDC. Much pushback from activist community who remember the scandal of 1992 when he overinterpreted data that he presented at the IAS meeting in Amsterdam on the Microgenesys gp 160 therapeutic vaccine data. He was investigated by the DoD and “cleared”; however, many thought that it was a white wash investigation. He is also recognized as being allied with right wing groups. He is an Opus Dei Catholic and early in the Pandemic, he pushed for mandatory testing and exclusion of infected people from the military.

I have supported his past 24 years of service at University of Maryland running their AIDS Clinic and being Deputy to Bob Gallo at the Institute for Human Virology. Stewart Simonsan working with Ladd Wiley and Bill Pierce as media advisors to Alex and Bob have asked me to help Bob out and “show him the ropes”.

Participate at another very enjoyable “Atlantic Live” panels at The Hamilton Restaurant (600 – 14th Street, NW) associated with showing of the film “Invisible Killers – Influenza” (part of a 3-part series with Influenza, Ebola and Smallpox). Panel moderator was Steve Clemons (Editor-at-Large of Atlantic). I was prominently featured in the film. Co-panelists were Inger Damon (CDC) and Loring Flint of Inova. Great venue – food and drinks with discussion.

Gave breakfast talk/panel discussion at Brazda Health Reporters Breakfast at APCO Worldwide headquarters at 1299 Pennsylvania Ave., NW. Spoke on Pandemic influenza. The flu cases are dramatically down and except for indication that as H3N2 is disapperaring, there are more cases of Influenza B. However, apart from that, flu is off the radar screen. Participated in the FDA/NIH leadership Council meeting in Building 1. Scott Gottlieb there. I spoke about Antibiotic Resistance.
Mumps outbreak in Delaware. I did interview on WTOP. Underlying problem is the waning immunity to Mumps vaccine. ACIP and CDC now recommend 3rd shot IF there is an outbreak, not routine 3rd shot.
Gave dinner speech (5 Presidents talk) followed by 40 minutes of questions at the Harvard Club at 555 - 13th Street, NW

Did all-day filming of me by Janet Tobias who will work for 2 years filming me at meetings, on travel, etc for a documentary she is doing on AIDS. Also in the documentary are Glenda Gray (RSA) and 2 others

Had the now usual meet and greet breakfast with Congressman Pete Sessions (R-TX) at the Capitol with Francis Collins and Nora Volkow. Pete is a great guy and loves me. This is the 5th one that we have done. We then rushed over to the Rayburn Building (see below). Testified at the House Appropriations Subcommittee Hearing for NIH Chaired by Rep. Tom Cole (R-OK). Very friendly Hearing. Also testifying was Collins, Ned Sharpless, Nora Volkow, Diana Bianchi. Went to a very crowded and extremely elegant reception at the home of George and Mari Will at sponsored by the Lerner family (Owners of Simonson who is now Assistant DG for administration at WHO. Signed and MOU with Tedros for collaborations. NIAID will soon become a WHO collaborating center.

Did a panel on vaccines at the Metropolitan Club at 1700 – H Street, NW chaired by Travis Brown (old friend from NCS/STA). Sponsored by UNICEF. Other panel members – author Steve Johnson and UNICEF official Robin Nandy. High- end club.

Went to Baltimore at invitation of Bob Gallo to give the 14th Annual Marlene and Stewart Greenebaum Lecture on “Emerging IDs” at the historic Westminster Church (burial place of Edgar Allen Poe). Had lunch at Uzo Bay restaurant. Good to see Bob. He is struggling with succession plan for the IHV and his own role in the coming years. He is 82 years old.

Interesting evening. Peter Staley and David Barr, my old ACT-UP New York and TAG friends came to dinner at my house with a new young activist, James Krellenstein. The purpose was to brainstorm how to get the price of Truvada down for use as PrEP. They have been getting nowhere with Gilead and so they are now pursuing a class action suit as well as thinking about civil disobedience. They came for my ideas and help. I served the usual sausages and rigatoni with a salad of cut peppers and Coppola Pinot Noir and Santa Marguerita Pinot Grigio. I offered to help by discussing this with Alex Azar. Also, I read to them (with tears in my eyes) the chapter in my book on Jim Hill. Jim Krellenstein is only 29 years old and I wanted him to learn some history of what things were like “back in the day”.

a4B7 work is not reproducd in our group with Jeff Lifson, Michele Demascio and Cliff Lane. Trying to figure out why. Trump and team continue to egregiously lie and it has become so commonplace that people do not even notice.
NAS Garden Party. Met Paul Farmer and entire Farmer family pluc Orphelia Dahl. Learned that my candidate Dennis Kasper finally got into the NAS. Yeah!!

Chaired Panel at Natcher Building for the 50th Anniversary of the Fogarty International Center. Fogarty’s family and virtually everyone profusely thanking me for “saving the FIC” by my comments to the House Committee last year. Also, the panel was extremely well-received – I chaired and on panel was Linda-Gail Becker, Bill Pape, Quaraisha Abdool Karim, and Sten Vermund.
Received the FDA Alumni Association Wiley Award at the Reagan Building and gave Plenary Lecture at their meeting

Flew to West Palm Beach to give the Opening Plenary at the 34th Annual Meeting of the ASM Clinical Virology Symposium and I received the Ed Nowakowski Award. Spoke on Universal Influenza Vaccine. Extremely well-received. Beautiful area – West Palm Beach.

Amazing day!! Went to Dallas on May 9 to participate in the celebration of the 15th Anniversay of PEPFAR. Invited by President George W. Bush. Took place at the George W. Bush Presidential Center. Mark Dybul and I were billed as the “architects” of PEPFAR. There were 2 panels for discussion. Both facilitated beautifully by Barbara Bush (daughter). First panel – Agnes Binaqwaho, Mark Dybul, Mike Gerson. Second panel – Paul Farmer, me, Senator Lindsey Graham, Favorite (Favo) Iradukunda (Ph.D nursing student from Rwanda). Excellent discussions – We all (including me) paid tribute to the POTUS who was somewhat embarrassed (and extremely modest) about his historic accomplishment with PEPFAR. Great part of the evening where we had a private dinner in the dining room of the Center with Potus, Laura and Barbara Bush, the entire panel, Kenneth A. Hersh (President and CEO of the George W. Bush Presidential Center, as well as some young fellows from Barbara’s Global Health Corps. She is stepping down after 10 years and is considering what her next challenge will be. Lazarus Effect Engage Moderator Q The discussions at dinner were amazing. Great conversations, including with Senator Graham describing his interactions with Trump. He believes that Trump is a good person who is an “unusual character” with an attention span measured in seconds to minutes at the most. George W. just listened and smiled and did not criticize, but it was clear that he was rolling his eyes. Graham is a terrific person and extremely funny and sharp. He is concerned about Syria and the suffering people. He is very compassionate conservative who is very moderate to left on immigration. He had just come from Arizonia where he visited his close friend Senator McCain who is ailing from glioblastoma, but is stable. . We discussed the issue of Israel likely confronting Iran and Trumps dissolving of the Iran nuclear deal. Amazing night. When we departed, I had a very warm goodbye to the POTUS. Gave a long hug and I said “I love you Mr. President”. He said: “Likewise, Fauci”. Flew back on May 10 and presented Anne Schuchat with the John P. Utz Leadership Award of the NFID at the NFID Gala at the Willard Hotel. Gave a very positive introduction for Anne. Met her mother who “idolizes” me.

Gave the Commencement Address to the School of Arts and Sciences at American University. The address was extremely well-received. Took place in Bender Arena of the Butler Pavillion. I joked with the audience saying that now that I have an honorary doctorate, I will not feel so guilty about using their men’s room when I run through the campus. Sylvia Burwell was delighted with my accepting the invitation to give the address as well as the address itself. That evening had dinner with Gepi Pantaleo at Café Milano. Franco Nuschese made a special menu for us. Just by chance that he was in the restaurant this night (Sunday – Mother’s Day).
Delivered AOA Lecture at Weill Cornell Medicine. Many nostalgic moments walking around the medical school and the building on York Avenue and East 69th-70th Street

With Francis Collins, I helped host the visit of Barbra Streisand, her husband James Brolin and her entourage to the NIH. It was a great visit and she was wonderful to all of us. I can now say after several encounters that she and I are friends. She gave the Ed Rall Cultural lecture and was interviewed by Collins on the stage of the Natcher Building. I thoroughly enjoyed her and particularly her husband Jim Brolin, father of actor Josh Brolin. Jim has won Golden Globe Awards for his TV performances as Marcus Welby, MD. He is a very modest man. Photo below

Gave remarks in the AM to the pre-opening Press briefing of the “Outbreak” exhibit at the National Museum of Natural History (Smithsonian). An exhibit on emerging infections that we at NIAID (me, David Morens and Jeff Taubenberger) provided material for. Photos of me, John Mascola and others. Great exhibit. Will run for 2 years and expects 3 million visits. Then on the road for a couple of years That evening had a very elegant reception for the opening of the above exhibit. MY entire front OD group attended: Cat, Hilary, Bob Eisinger, Courtney, Tara, etc.

The ebola outbreak still smoldering in DRC. Originated in Bikoro on Lake Tumba, but now there has been a case in Mbandaka that is a city of 1.2 million on the Congo River that connects with Kinshasa (DRC) and Brazzaville (Republic of the Congo) and so concern is that it could widely spread. At present 44 cases and 26 deaths. VSV vaccine being deployed for “Ring” vaccination. We will send VRC’s mAb114 for protocol distribution. All being done “differently” now in close coordination with WHO. We are being very good about working with Anna Mara Restrepo of WHO; formerly had friction with her during the West Africa outbreak. Much better relations now. Testified before the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee of the FY 2019 budget for NIH. Typical 2 hour hearing with Francis Collins, Ned Sharpless, Gary Gibbons, Nora Volkow, Richard Hodes and me. I got asked about universal flu vaccine, Ebola, Zika vaccine and FIC. Did long “photo shoot” with photographer (Jono Rattman) from The Atlantic for upcoming story they will be doing on me.

Went to Boston to give Commencement Address at Boston University Medical School. Voted as choice to speak by the students. Interesting history. Melissa (Molly) Pritchard graduated today. She used to do sleep-overs in my house with Megan when she was 3 years old and then she worked in the LIR for a couple of years. Now she is graduating medical school. Speech very well received. Arrived the night before to have dinner at Moona Restaurant in Cambridge with Jenny and Christina. Stopped off to see Lucca in Jen’s apartment.

Chris and my 33th Anniversary!!! Taped a long segment for CBS Sunday Morning on food allergy. To air in June. Chris and I went to Casalare restaurant for celebratory dinner.

Went to Boston to receive Doctor of Science, honoris causa from Boston University. Arrived Saturday (May 19), saw Jenny, Christina and Lucca, had dinner at BU President’s home. Went to Boston Pops to hear a medley of Leonard Bernstein works. It was terrific. I thought that it would be a boring concert since I did not know it was LB. It was great. Next day (Sunday, 20 May) had ceremony. Keynote Speaker and also honorary doctorate was John Lewis. He was inspirational and the crowd loved him. Also receiving honorary degrees were: Zhang Yimou (Chinese film producer who did the opening and closing of Beijing Olympics), Carmen Yulín Cruz Soto (Mayor of San Juan who conflicted with Trump during Hurricanes), and Vibha Bakshi (famous Indian journalist). Beautiful day in Boston. Good time. It was clear that very few students at the college level really know who I am whereas everyone knew John Lewis and he deservedly stole the show. Also, the Chinese and Chinese-American students (about 25% of the class) all knew Zhang Yimou.

Gave talk and panel discussion at the ASM Conference on “Outbreak” in association with the National Museum of Natural History exhibit (see above). I spoke on Influenza and a Universal Influenza Vaccine. Other panelists – Nancy Messonier (CDC), Mary Wooley (Research Amer!ca). Chair – Stefano Bertuzzi (ASM). Event at the Newseum. Received a letter (May 16, 2018) from Oly Ilunga Kalenga, MOH of the DRC asking me to send him our mAb114 against Ebola for use during the outbreak. The mAb was developed by the VRC derived from a patient from the Kikwit, DRC outbreak in 1995. VRC brought the patient here and cloned B cells to develop mAb. It is very powerful and requires only 1 dose; is lyophilized and so does not need strict cold chain. I wrote back and said we would make it available to him as long as we do this with coordination of the WHO in accordance with the new approach towards transparency and coordination.

Did teleconference presentation (me in Bethesda; they is Palo Alto) to the Science Philanthropy Alliance to present my strategic planning process for a Universal Influenza Vaccine in order to get money for the project. This organization is formed by Larry and Lucy (Lucinda) Page. Larry is CEO of Google and wants to donate money for science, particular interest in influenza. I could not physically go to Palo Alto because of Congressional hearing that will take place tomorrow. Group (n = 40) of GOP House members wrote a letter to Trump asking him not to re- appoint Francis Collins as NIH Director. They claim that he promotes stem cell and fetal tissue research. Also, that he campaigned for Obama.

Served on panel at the Wall Street Journal Health Forum at the Four Seasons Hotel. My panel was chaired by Betsy McKay of WSJ and co-panelist was Anne Schuchat (CDC). Topic was “Gone Viral? Tracking Epidemics”

entries.content: Gave a briefing on Universal influenza vaccine to the NIH Senate Caucus at the Russell Senate Office Building on behalf of “Act for NIH” (Pat White). Senators Dick Durbin and Lindsey Graham attended. Big crowd of Senate Staffers.

Briefed Secretary Azar in his HHS conference room on tuberculosis. This is part of the increasing momentum re: TB. Stll unclear whether I will be attending the UNGASS meeting on TB in Sept. Also, this is part of multiple briefings of Azar.

Went to Boston to celebrate the 75th birthday of Dennis Kasper with a sumposium in his honor at the Joseph Martin Conference Center. Then went to the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum for reception/dinner. Dennis was very moved that I attended and I gave the opening plenary lecture. Jenny not in Boston. She actually was in DC. I see her tomorrow at home.

I receive the Katherine B. Gebbie Lifetime Achievement Award for Outstanding Federal Service given to a previous winner of the Arthur Flemming Award that I won in 1979 (Yikes!). Ceremony at GWU Marvin Center

I was on a panel discussing the showing of “Bending the Arc”, the documentary of the creation and work of Partners in Health by Paul Farmer, Jim Kim, and Orphelia Dahl. Took place at the NAS on 21st Street, NW and sponsored by Victor Dzau and the NAM. Jim Kim and Deb Birx were on the panel with me.

Spoke at the New Hampshire Business Day event in the Hart Building at

the invitation of Senator Shaheen (D-NH). She sent me a nice thank you letter:

DOC334.pdf
Annual Garden Party at the home of Jamie Gorelick and Rich Waldron. Have been going to this for years. Usual A list there: Chris Matthews, Merrick Garland, etc.
Bob Redfield (new CDC Director) visited NIH and Francis Collins and I showed him around the VRC; then I gave him a tour of the SCSU in the Clinical Center.

I testified before the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations on “Biopreparedness”. Also testifying: Anne Schuchat (CDC), Denise Hinton (FDA), and Rick Bright of BARDA. Very friendly Hearing. Congresswoman Anna Eshoo (D-CA) surprised me and the hearing room when she said that” “I have no questions of Dr. Fauci, but I want to say that he should be canonized”. She then went on with effusive praise of me and my career. Very nice.

Was on a panel of the US Global Leadership Coalition at Grand Hyatt Hotel in DC to celebrate the 15th Anniversary of PEPFAR. On panel was Josh Bolten, Mark Dybul, Deb Birx, Congresswoman Barbara Lee and Sen. Tom Daschle. Josh was clear in giving me credit for putting the program together.

Attended another typical Catherine and Wayne Reynolds dinner at the Jefferson Hotel. Truly the A list there. Chatted and had fun with old acquantances: Colin Powel, Bret Baier (Fox News), Brendan Sullivan, Merrick Garland, Justice Anthony Kennedy, Fred Hiatt, Rick Atkinson, Eric Holder, Sharon Malone, Wolf Blitzer, Rita Braver, etc Amazing entertainer at end of evening – Rhiannon Giddens.
Chris and I did a 2 person “panel” at a reception/fund raiser for the Children’s Inn at the Bethesda Country Club. We told the story of our meeting and our NIH experiences.

Was on WTOP talking about the poor efficacy of seasonal flu vaccines. Also, went down to HHS to discuss which of the Zika vaccines we should try to take to licensure. BARDA has run out of money and so we need to either ask for more or push the pharmaceutical companies (PaxVax – DNA vaccine and Takeda - PIV) to pony up more.

Brett Giroir (Assiatant Secretary for Health, HHS) called me and wants me to join him and Bob Redfield in an attempt to put something together to go to Alex Azar with to “End the USA AIDS Pandemic”. This is exactly what I tried to do during the Obama administration with Valerie Jarrett and Ceclia Munoz and Doug Brooks. We did not get much traction since it was clear that there was no new money.

Had phone conversation with Brett Giroir and Bob Redfield and George Sigounas (HRSA) and Michael Weahkee of the HIS regarding the End of AIDS plan (see above). I will send them the original plan that we drew up for the Obama administration. I will send the original plan and a 2018 update. Brett gave answers to the rhetorical question of “Why now?”: 1) Spectacular success of ART as TasP; 2) Success of PrEP; 3) Epidemiology – small # of USA counties accounting for majority of infections; 4) Proven models – PEPFAR, PMI, Global Fund, etc.; 5) Right people/right time: ASF, Bob Redfield, Dep Sec, Sec. Azar, Joe Grogan in OMB Met with people that Mark Dybul brought by who are working for a company that is working towards a cure for HIV as well as a vaccine. The lead scientist was Dr. Serhat Gumrkcu, a Turkish physician and Gregory Howell, his assistant (?). The company they work for is Enochian. I gave them some advice for future directions Also, spoke with Dr. Cameron from Canada who is doing an a4B7 study. He is seeing some diminution of set point virus. The virus rebounds, but at a lower set point.

Received a nice note from President George W. Bush dated June 20, 2018 thanking me for participating in the PEPFAR event in Dallas

Others speakers (I was the official eulogizer) were: James Kazura (Case Western), Ken Frazier (Merck), Bonnie Bassler and Tom Shenk (Princeton). I spoke of “Growing up with Adel in academic medicine”. Incredibly hot. 100 degrees F in Princeton with no air conditioning in the Chapel.

Met at AAAS headquarters on 12th St, NW and NY Avenue with the ad hoc Working Group – “Rescuing Biomedical Research” led by Harold Varmus, Bruce Alberts, Shirley Tilghman, Keith Yamamoto, etc. They called together a group of IC Directors (me, Jon Lorsch, Nora Volkow, Mike Lauer, Larry Tabak (Deputy NIH Director). Struggling with how to get early stage investigators (ESIs) funded and turn around the anxiety among young scientists about getting funded.

Things have been relatively quiet. Trump still acting erratically crazy about almost everything. Had a teleconference with HHS (Bob Kadlec) led by Eric Hargan on “Sepsis”. I presented what NIH is doing on research on sepsis, CDC also presented. My concern is that Bob Kadlec seems obsessed with the concept of terrorists utilizing tactics that would mimic sepsis (metabolic dyregulators). I love Bob, but from the beginning of this administration he focuses more on bioterrorists than on naturally occurring outbreaks – just the opposite of me.

Delivered my memoir to Rick Atkinson at a private dinner he and I had at Matisse Restaurant. Rick has been amazingly helpful. He offered to bring copies of the book to his editor John Sterling and his agent Rafe (Raphael) Sagalyn to read without any strings attached. A couple of days later, I also dropped off a copy of the book to Bill Shultz at his home at Bill will read manuscript during his vacation on Nantucket. Rick told me a few days later that he really likes the manuscript. He is about 25% through it.
Off to Amsterdam for the IAS meeting. Will make 4 presentations including a major plenary.
Highly successful IAS meeting in Amsterdam. My 4 talks went extremely well, particularly my Plenary Lecture on July 25. Back now to catch up.

Bret Giroir has submitted to the small group of Bret, Bob Redfield, George Sigounas, and Mike Weahkee a plan to consider to present to Alex Azar to go to the POTUS with the initiative/plan to end the epidemic in the USA. I modified the plan somewhat and Bret accepted all changes. We are to discuss this week. See plan below: ASFR-Ending Aids in America 7.30.18 v5
Did BBC Radio interview on the control of Ae.Aegypti mosquitoes in Australia by Wolbachia infection.
Got realistic assessment of my memoir manuscript from Rick Atkinson and his editor John Sterling. See below note from Rick. FAUCI NOTE, 2 Aug. 2018.docx

Did Skype TV interview with NBC-2 on Zika vaccine trial. Much craziness going on with Trump who continually denies any Russian involvement in the election despite that fact that all intelligence agencies are openly saying that there is no doubt that Russia interfered. Met with a group of activists led by Paul Kawata of the National Minority AIDS Coalition. Also, Jesse Milan of AIDS United, Murray Penner of NASTAD, Mike Ruppal of the AIDS Institute, David Harvey of the National Coalition of STD Directors. This is the context of the Ending the AID Epidemic that we are doing with Brett Giroir. They have heard about it and are concerned since they have heard that I am not a part of it. They do not trust this Administration and they feel that it cannot succeed unless I lead it. I assured them that I am very much a part of it , but I cannot say much more. The HHS group (Brett, Bob Redfield, George Sigounas, Mike Weahkee, et al) meets with DepSec Eric Horgan next week.

Briefed Secretary Azar on the TB initiative that we (NIH, CDC, FDA, OGA) are putting together. It calls for $~3 billion each for CDC and NIH. Alex likes the initative, but indicated that there was really no new money. I knew that all along. The initative is one of several that are being suggested for possibility to include in the SOTU address. Francis Collins and Larry Tabak met with Alex right after I did and Francis did not know about the initiative and so got annoyed that I did not tell him since Alex brought it up in the meeting with Francis. I had not told Francis since I knew that it was a non-starter. Also, I thought that NIAID budget people had informed OSD budget people.

Cliff and I met with Jeremy Farrar (Wellcome Trust -WC) at HHS and also had dinner with him and Garrett Grigsby, Rick Bright, and Ed Whiting (Chief-of- staff) to Jeremy) about how NIAID and WC can work together in the future. Clearly our relationship is markedly improved compared to the West Africa Ebola times.

Went to Boston to see Jenny (her 32 Birthday!!) and to Provincetown to see Jim Dickson and Vivian. Took PTown ferry from Boston. Great time with Jim who is 94 years old. He was totally delighted that I finally visited him.

Two meeting at HHS. 1) Ebola follow-up with Bob Kadlec and ASPR group. We are in the 2nd DRC outbreak in a few months. Right after the 2017 outbreak was declared over, within days, we have another outbreak in the Kivu section of the country (Northeast) and Beni as opposed to the 2017 outbreak in the Western part of the DRC. 57 cases so far. 2) Meeting with DEPSEC Eric Hargan to present to Giroir.Fauci/Redfield/Weahkee/Sigounas plan to “End HIV AIDS in the USA”. Eric was cautious and although sympathetic to and interested in what we are trying to do, he was concerned that this was potentially dilute and interfere with the ongoing Opioid Crisis initiative of the USG. We will get more budget numbers and meet again, hopefully in anticipation of presenting to Alex. I still feel that we should squeeze Gilead to lower the price of Truvada.

Spoke with Peter Staley by phone to get insight into how to approach the Truvada price question to convince Giroir that we need to do this. Peter wants to be aggressive and either break the Gilead patent, have NIH do “march in” or make Truvada generic now. It officially becomes generic in 2021. Peter mentioned that NY State give free starter packs of Truvada for people coming into STD clinics. They then get hooked up to the health system that assumes the cost of the drug through insurance. I will write to Brett Giroir to discuss.

Busy day. Did 2 segments on WTOP on 1) Food allergy, and 2) Vaccines for children before they return to school in the context of the anti-vax people. Did a podcast for Michael Morell on his new podcast “Intelligence Matters”. Spoke about ID outbreaks – deliberate and naturally occurring. Mike is the Former Deputy Director of CIA and acting Director of CIA under George Bush. Great interview. Briefed Sec. Azar on Ebola in DRC. Situation getting worse with increase in cases and trouble doing contact tracing due to the danger from terrorists/militias/rebels. Multiple rebellious militia operating around the outbreak area – the city of Beni. We have sent mAb 114 as a treatment. mAb 114 was developed by the NIAID VRC from a patient from DRC who recovered from the 1995 Kikwit outbreak. We brought him to NIH and cloned his B cells to make the mAB. As of yesterday 5 patients treated with 114. Unlike the West Africa outbreak, this time there is good collaboration with WHO and an understanding about what research is.

(Friday) – Was supposed to be Keynote Speaker at the Inaugural Richard B. Marchese Scientific Symposium at the University of Alabama (invited by Mike Saag). Mechanical difficulty of plane had me cancel trip and go back to NIH to do the talk by “Go To Meeting”. Went well. Good thing I cancelled since the flight that would have gotten me back to DC that night was cancelled and I would have been stuck in Alabama until Saturday afternoon. Things heating up in DRC with Ebola. Infections in areas with rebel activity.

Bob Redfield in DRC. Called me at home (Sunday night). He is stuck at Entebbe airport on way home. He described to me in detail the situation on the ground in DRC. Rebel activity is a problem in getting to the exposed and contacts. We are trying to get a randomized clinical trial (without placebo) comparing multiple therapies. 10 people have received the mAb 114 from VRC. Reports are that they are all alive, but we have nothing to compare them to.

Call with me, Cliff and Jeremy Farrar. Jeremy is now in agreement with us that WHO despite their “good intentions” is really an obstacle to getting clinical trials and good information. We are working to get AD26 vaccine also given with the VSV (PREVAC trial that Cliff is now doing in West Africa (Liberia, Guinea, Sierra Leone and Mali). Also, Jeremy agrees we need to do randomized (non placebo) trials for therapies. Met with Alex Azar 1-0n-1. He wanted a scientific update on AIDS, Influenza, etc. Also, wanted to make sure that I am OK, happy, no one is bothering me, etc. Good man, but he likes Trump and ignores the craziness that is going on in the WH.

Testified at the Senate HELP Committee chaired by Lamar Alexander and Ranking Minority Mike Bennet (D-CO). Other ICs besides Collins were Diana Bianchi, Richard Hodes, Ned Sharpless. Reviewed 21 Century Cure Act. Discussed Chinese stealing our IT and research data via Chinese post-docs getting paid by China at same time they are funded by NIH. Big investigations by FBI on the way. I got asked only 1 question by Bennet regarding “what worries me the most” – pandemic flu.

Trump getting into trouble and many people are flipping and asking for immunity – his Lawyer Cohen, his financial person, etc. Republicans are losing all their dignity by not speaking up against Trump who is acting more and more erratic. Did interviews with NPR “Science Friday” with Ira Flatow on Ebola and TV interview on ABC7 (Local) on timing of flu shots. Sad and unfortunate occurrence. My old friend and former CDC Director Tom Frieden was arrested and put in handcuffs today in NYC for allegedly groping a woman whom he has known for 30 years in his home after having dinner last October (2017) with Tom’s wife, the woman and her husband. The charges are inappropriate groping 3rd degree sexual harassment and 1st degree harassment. Apparently, he was “harassing her” when she decided months later (April) to write a blog about the experience without naming him. That triggered the complaint and arrest. Very sad. Will clearly hurt his outstanding career no matter how this sorts out.

Interview with BBC World Services on the efficacy of mAb 114 now given to 12 people and all are alive. I had to temper the claims (apparently by Tedros of WHO) that this is a Transforming and historic breakthrough. If we declare a “cure”, we will never able to definitively show it works in a clinical trial unless almost everyone who gets it does well. Stay tuned.

Had dinner at my home with Jonathan (Jono) Mermin of CDC. He was in DC for some meetings with Congressional staff. Jono is Director of the Center for HIV/AIDS, STD, Hepatitis C, and TB prevention. Just me, Jono and Chris. Great evening. Jono is a terrific guy. We spoke mostly about how we can work together on the “End AIDS in the USA” initiative that Brett Geroir is coordinating.

Has meeting in my office with Raphael (Rafe) Sagalyn who is Rick Atkinson’s ong-time agent for his books. Great meeting concerning the way forward for my book. Rafe read it and liked it, but said (as Sterling and Rick have) that it needs an editor if it is to have wide acceptance. He feels strongly that it has the makings of a best seller. Had call with Bill Steiger (now of USAID) who wants to transfer some USAID Ebola money to me and NIAID since they cannot spend all of the original Ebola supplement from 2015-16. We are now working this out to determine possibility In the meantime, Ebola still active in DRC. 121 cases and 81 deaths. Security is still an issues with rebels attacking peacekeepers and killing them. Now 13 people have received mAb 114 and 11 have been discharged. Looking good, but still not in an RCT. Also, 6 have received Remdesivir.

Had conference call with Jeremy Farrar (Wellcome Trust), Yves Levy (INSERM), Cliff Lane, and people from European Commission to determine how we can coordinate our research/clinial trials. Jeremy being helpful, but I sense that the EC is having issues with source of funding.

great trip to San Francisco and then to Point Reyes on a “family gathering” with Chris and I from DC, Ali in SF, Megan from NOLA, and Jenny from Boston. Rented a Cabin in Point Reyes/Petuloma. Beautiful hikes, family talks, hot tub, happy hours, restaurants. Great bonding. Unfortunately, Jenny lost her wallet on the last day, but she was a champ about it and did not decompensate.

Outbreaks of meales in Europe (Ukraine, Serbia, Italy, France, etc.) due to anti-vax movement. Did TV interview with BBC focusing on Italy, whose parliament just passed law that said families cannot be required to vaccinate their children before they go to school. Bad, bad idea!

I served as the presiding official (Retired Rear Admiral, USPHS) at the formal retirement of my friend and colleague, Colonel Nelson Michael. I gave the laudation and then officially retired him at WRAIR in Silver Spring. Went to a roast of him at the Army-Navy Club at Farrugat Square in DC Did interview on WTOP on influenza vaccines

DEPSEC Eric Hargan came to Fisher’s Lane to the Biovisualization Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality facility for a demonstration. I hosted him with Mike Tartakovsky. Eric was delighted as he virtually “walked into” hemagglutinin and HIV envelope moelcules. Meet with Skip Virgin and group from Viir including CEO George Scangos in 7A-18. Also present were NIAID Divisions Directors John Mascola, Carl Dieffenbach, Emily Erbelding and several IRP scientists. Very likely and optimistic that we will develop several collaborations with them, particularly in the arena of developing mAbs against various pathogens. My regular intermittent dinner with Larry Corey (present at Viir meeting) at Matisse restaurant.
Did taped interview for an educational program given by the Council on Foreign Relations at the HQ on 17th and F Streets, NW. Sylvia Burwell also participating in the program.
Chris and I went to the Annual Welcome the Fall affair at the home of Calvin and Jane Cafritz on Usual A Crowd there and very pleasant and totally elegant.

Outbreak of Ebola still smoldering in DRC. We have administered 14 treaments of mAb114 – still no deaths. Still trying to get a RCT going comparing mAb114 to Remdesivir and ZMAPP. Cliff will go to Kinshasa on Sunday (Sept. 16) to try and move things along. Trump still acting crazy. Bob Woodward’s book “Fear”Trump in the White House” came out with a splash juxtaposed with the NY Times Op-Ed (anonymous) from a few days ago written by a senior WH Official saying that the Trump WH is totally dysfunctions and that Trump is unhinged. Did VOA on mAb114.
Did CBS Radio News on imminent seasonal influenza.

Had a full day with David Rubenstein (Founder and Co-CEO of the Carlyle Group). He interviewed me at a lunch panel at the annual meeting of Carlyle Investors at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel (22nd St, NW) Also on the the panel were Mary Klotman (Duke) and Paul Rothman (Hopkins). Big crowd of investors at lunch. That evening, David invited me to a VIP table for a dinner at the Washington Hilton where he interviewed on Stage before 1100 people Jeff Bezos. Jeff had just announced a $2 billion donation for homeless people and for early education. Big push to get Bezos to put a new Amazon Headquarters in Washington, DC. The interview by David of Bezos was amazing. It was an interesting autobiography of Bezos brought out by Danid’s interviewing skills. At my table was Judy Woodruff and Candi Wolf, formerly of VP Cheney.
Did WJLA ABC Channel 7 TV on the upcomiong flu season. Gave panel presentation at Congressional Black Caucus at DC Convention Center for Rep. Barbara Lee (D-CA).

Chris and I visited Mark Dybul and Jason Claire at their beautiful home on the Eastern Shore (Chestertown, MD) for a day of relaxation. They built an amazing home right on the edge of the water of the Chesapeake Bay. Mark lives there most of the year despite his appointment at Georgetown. He works from home, travels much and goes to Georgetown 2-3 days per month.

Gave talk and panel discussion on TB at the State Department (Diplomacy Center of the Harry Truman Building). Chris Collins (of Friends of the Global Fund) chaired the session. Other panelists: Irene Goek (USAID), Hank Thomlinson (CDC) and Ed Cox (FDA). Garret Grigsby (OGA-HHS) gave closing remarks. This is all in anticipation of the High Level Meeting (HLM) of the UN Special Session of TB next week, which I will attend.

Made a presentation and served on a panel in the Russell Senate Office Building, Kennedy Caucus Room to celebrate the 15th year anniversary of PEPFAR. Also participating were: Deb Birx, Mark Dybul, Seah Callahan (Catholic Relief Services. Sponsoroed by Senator Johnny Isakson. Deb made generous discussion of my key role in the creation of PEPFAR. Received the Leadership Award from the Friends of Cancer (Ellen Sigal) at the Rooftop of the Hay Adams Hotel. Award presented to me by Secretary Alex Azar. Great evening. Other winner was Rick Klausner. Sean Parker was present. Wonderful videos honoring Rick and me. Great dinner afterwards. Embarrassingly flattering of me.

Met with Deputy Director General of WHO Dr. Soumya Swaminathan in 7A-18. Soumya is an old friend from India. We discussed the issues that Cliff is dealing with regarding the sometimes obstructive actions of WHO in the area of research during outbreaks (esp. Anna Maria Restrepo).

(Sunday) – Flew to NYC for a Satellite meeting of the UN High Level Meeting (HLM) on TB. Held at 75 Rockefeller Plaza. It was a Stop TB meeting. I was on a panel with Paul Stoffels. Went very well. I spoke about our TB Strategic Plan. That we will put online on Sept.26.
Had very good conversation with CDC (Nancy Messonnier and Dan Jernigan on how NIH and CDC can develop a consistent message for the upcoming influenza season.

Went to NYC for several functions at the UN HLM on TB. On Tuesday night (6:00 PM) went to the CDC Foundation AMR event. Present were Secretary Azar, WHO DG Tedros, among others. Then went to Partners in Health and Unitade Receptions at the Rooftop of the Library Hotel. Met with Paul Farmer and Jim Kim among others. On September 26 (Wed) I represented the USA and sat in the USA seat for a panel of the General Assembly. I gave a 2 minute presentation describing our research effort and announcing that our Strategic Plan and my JAMA paper on the Plan went online at 10:00 AM. After my presentation, Co-Chair of the Panel, Dr. David Sergeenko thanked me and publicly said that it was “an honor to have Dr. Fauci with us today”. Also, had lunch with Secertary Azar, Jeremy Farrar (Wellcome Trust), Bob Redfield, Garret Grigsby, Ed Whiting (Farrar Chief-of-Staff). Alex trying to foster collaboration between NIAID and WT. Met with Republic of the Congo Minister of Health Jacqueline Mikolo and discussed potential collaborations with NIAID and ROC. Vincent Munster of RML is already collaborating. Also, that evening (Sept. 26) was on panel at a CDC Foundation function at the Grand Hyatt. Gave 3 minute presentation on our research agenda and again announced the Plan that was put ONLINE today. Got enthusiastic response from the audience.

Gave Plenary Lecture on final day of “Outbreak Week” symposium given by the Harvard Global Health Institute taking place at the Harvard Law School in Cambridge. Spoke on Pandemic Preparedness. Great audience including the usual global health people. Also, Ron Klain, Mosoka Fallah from Liberia (worked with Cliff on PREVAIL). Very well received. Several days later, I saw the video of Ron Klain’s lunch presentation (I had to leave to go back to DC and so I missed his presentation). Ron spoke about outbreak response and when he came to the issue of communications under stressful circumstances, he said that the White House learned quickly that during the Ebola outbreak they had a special way of handling communications crises. They call it PTFOT – Put Tony Fauci on television! That evening, went with Chris to the Jefferson Hotel for a dinner hosted by Roy Pfautch (Republican Global Affairs Consultant) in honor of Professor Yoshitake Yokokura, President of the World Medical Association (WMA). I had met him in Chicago when I gave Plenary Lecture at the WMA meeting last year. Sat next to Senator Bill Cassidy (R-LA). Friendly conversation, but remember, he is the one with whom I dueled at a Congressional Hearing 2 years ago about his wanting to cut money for HIV/AIDS. All of Washington (and the country) is ablaze about the Hearing pitting Dr. Christine Blasey Ford against Judge Brett Kavanaugh. Kavanaugh did poorly and even insulted some of the Senators during the questioning.

Gave presentation to the Bio CEOs on Vaccines and public-private partnerships at their headquarters on 1201 Maryland Avenue, SW This evening attended and made remarks at book signing reception at The Homer Building on 13th Street, NW for Tommy Thompson and his book “Tommy: My Journey of a Lifetime”. All of the old crew was there from Tommy’s days at HHS: Scooter Libby, Kevin Keane, Joe Grogan, Eric Hargan, Bob Wood, Peter Urbanowicz, Bill Pierce. Also, had nice conversation with Reince Priebus about his tenure in the Trump administration. I told some funny Tommy stories about our trips to Africa, the 9/11 episode of when he told me to go to ground zero and represent HHS, etc.

Went to book signing event at the Decatur House in DC for a book written by Michael Beschloss entitled “Presidents of War”. Event sponsored by David Rubenstein, Andrea Mitchell and Alan Greenspan, Kate and Jim Lehrer, Mary Graham, Laura and Tim O’Shaughnessy, and Afsaneh Beschloss. Great reception. Usual Washington, DC “A” list present. Beschloss had been working on the book for 10 years! 700+ pages. Very enjoyable evening. FBI investigation of Brett Kavanaugh and Dr. Ford ending and Republicans in Senate are ruching to push the vote through. Many people coming forth and telling press that Kavanaugh was a sloppy drunk and that he lied under oath about how much he drank as a youth and other things. Trump publicly mocking Dr. Ford at a rally in Mississippi. Amazing!!
Kavanaugh approved by Senate 50-48. Profound division throughout the country. Trump continues to talk nonsense, inaccuracies and outright lies. Sad state of affairs in the country.

Since Tom Frieden’s Court Hearing is on Oct. 11, 2018 (2 days from now) I sent an e-mail to Tom wishing him well and telling him that I am thinking about him. He responded saying how grateful he was that I reached out to him and that he remembers how I stood up for him during the Ebola outbreak in 2014-2015.

Presented the keynote at the NIAID DAIDS “Strategies for a Cure” meeting at the Natcher Building and updated my talk on ART-Free-remissions that I gave at the IAS meeting in Amsterdam in July, 2018. Very well-received by the audience. Am now pushing hard on the concept of antibodies binding with virus after ATIs or after infection (if bNAbs) are present at the time of infection forming immune complexes that induce CD8+ T cells that durably control HIV. Ebola outbreak in DRC not well controlled with 4-5 cases coming per day (~62% mortality). Security is a big problem (rebel groups attacking responders). Cliff (travelling to Geneva multiple times) still trying hard to get a randomized (non-placebo) trial comparing mAb114 versus Remdesivir versus ZMAPP. WHO and their consultants continue to get in the way of getting the trial going with people with little or no clinical trial experience slowing things down asking for ridiculous limbs on the protocol. Oxford group a big problem (Horby). Jeremy Farrar now becoming a good ally.

Went to Baltimore in a driving rainstorm to give the Key note at the NASTAD HIV and Hepatitis meeting at Renassance Hotel. Audience are mostly providers. I still cannot get over the fact that most look upon me as an “icon” or “legend” – multiple people wanting “Selfies”.

Met with Mike McCune (in town for the Cure meeting). He now works for BMGF and wants to see me about a “network” of thinkers that he wants to put together to re-imagine how we approach HIV research. Also, Bill Gates feels that we cannot continue to approach the masses of HIV-infected people in the developing world the way we do. Bill has always been skeptical about treatment as prevention and PrEP solving the problem. He wants the field to figure out how we can give a single intervention to an infected person (not ART) that essentially “cures” them. Aspirational example is the develop a CRISPR-like approach that would convert a person to CCR5 negative in a single shot. Quite aspirational. I told Mike that I would be interested in further discussions. Had a very important meeting with Malcom Martin. He sowed me data where he infected NHPs with SHIV and gave them only bNAbs (3BNC117 and 10-1074 and their virus went down slowly and stayed down in 4 of 6 animals whereas untreated animals (as usual) went on to established set point viremia. Another bit of evidence about my theory of immune compelxes being formed and inducing immunity that durably controls viremia.

Had phone call with Larry Corey about the AMP study in Africa and my theory that those who received VRC01 and who nonetheless got infected might actually form the immune complexes with the VRC01 that is on board and the virus that emerges after infection. I told him that we should do a study of an ATI on all these infected people (from the untreated versus the trerated VRC01 group) to see whether those who received VRC01 had developed an immune response that controls the viremia. Also, in future vaccine studies that induce bNAbs, but the subjects nonetheless get infected, we should definitely do ATI studies on them and see if vaccination that did not protect against acquisition of infection actually induced immunity that durably controls virus. I will be pursuing this approach in our lab. Important event this afternoon/evening - Christine Grady gets formally inducted into the National Academy of Medicine (NAS), formerly the Institute of Medicine (IOM). A much-deserved honor!!!

First child dies of Influenza this season (in Florida – Influenza B). Also 127 cases of Acute Flaccid Myelitis (AFM) reported now in 127 children in 22 states thus far this year. First outbreaks in 2014 and 2016. First felt to be due to Enterovirus D68. However, really no definite etiology. Thought to be post-infectious. Incidence 1/1,000,000. For both of these, I appeared on WJLA Channel 7 local TV and tomorrow (Oct. 17) on WTOP Radio.
In addition to the WTOP appearance, I did FOX Channel 25 local TV on AFM. Also taped a segment for tonight with Doreen Gentzler at NBC News on AFM. Also, SPUTNIK (Russion News Service) print.

Much press interest in AFM. Did FOX 5 TV for the early morning show today on AFM. Did FOX 5 TV again, this time on influenza, for the evening show. Key issues evolving around the Ebola outbreak in DRC. Currently 220 cases and 142 deaths. Fifty percent of cases are not linked to a contact and this is very disturbing since it means that we are not able to do proper contact tracing. This relates to the very difficult security issues in the North Eastern region of Beni where rebel groups are attacking Health Care Workers. Cliff Lane is developing a protocol to test in a non-placebo randomized trial a comparison of ZMAPP versus mAb 114 versus Remdesivir. WHO still delaying things and getting in the way. Cliff going to Kinshasa over the weekend with a team to train Congolese in the conduct of trial and collection of data. Continued problem with MSF in that they refuse to administer IV fluids since they claim that their results have indicated that people do just as well (or badly) with IV versus oral – which is preposterous.

Summary of important issues! The Ebola outbreak in Northeast DRC is getting out of control in that contact tracing is being severely hindered by the rebel activity which is now attacking health care workers. It is possible that it will spread out of DRC and into other countries in the region such as Uganda, Rwanda, and South Sudan. The latest count of cases is 266 cases and 168 deaths. Some form of anti-Ebola medication has been given to 93 of these people. Great frustration on our part (with Cliff) in the delay in getting an RCT going with ZMAPP as the “control” since it is the only countermeasure that has been shown to be safe and that has shown some efficacy (albeit not statistically significant) against a placebo. Obstacles are MSF that is inherently against the design of the study thinking incorrectly that we are trying to show only that ZMAPP works, which could not be further from the truth since we believe (but need to prove) that mAb 114 is probably the best of the 3 drugs being uses (ZMAPP, Remdesivir, mAb 114) (also possibly Regeneron mAb). Also, USAID are being obstructionistic claiming that we should not be doing “research” during an outbreak and that we should concentrate on vaccinating contacts. In typical USAID fashion, they are being self-serving and in this case obstructionistic. In contrast, Bob Redfield and CDC are offering to help us in any way possible to get the RCT going. Also, Paul Stoffels and Janssen (J & J) are manipulating to get their Ebola vaccine into play (Ad26Ebola + MVA boost). We are testing their vaccine in our PREVAC trial, which is a placebo controlled VSV versus Ad26Ebola in West Africa. Paul is a good guy and a friend, but he is likely getting pressure from his board to get the vaccine tested in the outbreak. This is somewhat of a contradiction since the vaccine is a 2 dose (prime/boost at day 56) that is not appropriate for an outbreak and is only suited to pre- vaccinating HCWs and at-risk people. Nonetheless, Paul is agitating to get the vaccine in play. We will try to work it out since he is a good guy. MSF remains a problem. They do not appreciate the nuances of clinical trials and they want to have the option if someone does not want to go into the trial in a given Ebola treatment Unit (ETU), then they want to option of giving compassionate use administration of their drug of choice. This violates all the pricniples of an RCT. In any given ETU, it is either all RCT or all comnpassionate use. I had a conversation with Joanne Liu (President of MSF) at the DNDi event in NYC and although she means well, she insists that MSF have that option. Also, she believes that since we are making ZMAPP the “control” for the reasons given above, that we are favoring ZMAPP. It is tough getting through to her. Cliff is extremely frustrated in dealing with MSF since he feels (and I agree) that MSF are very brave in going into dangerous areas, but they do not give optimal care (they refuse to give IV fluids to Ebola patients since they believe that patients do as well or not with oral!!!!) This is totally nonsense. Also, they really do not understand clinical research. Since we need to deal with them, this is really a difficult situation.

Dr. He Jiankui (China) did a CRISPR editing of twin embryos editing out CCR5. The father was HIV positive, but the sperm was washed and the father was on ARVs with undetectable viral load. Mother uninfected. Therefore no chance of children (twins in this case) becoming infected in utero. The purpose of the editing out of CCR5 was declared by the authors to be the protect the children throughout life from getting infected with HIV. I consider this egregious unethical. There was a groundswell of push back from the scientific community. I was quoted in Science by Jon Cohen as saying: “The underlying purpose of doing the experiment was obviously to show that they could do gene editing on an embryo, but the purpose for the party involved does not make any sense,” says Anthony Fauci, an HIV/AIDS researcher who heads the U.S. National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases in Bethesda, Maryland. “There are so many ways to adequately, efficiently, and definitively protect yourself against HIV that the thought of editing the genes of an embryo to get to an effect that you could easily do in so many other ways in my mind is unethical.”

Major uptake by press with explicit referrals to my role in the initiative: virtually all print outlets, Mike Gerson in Wash Post, Jon Cohen in Science. Excerpts from my press conference today run on PBS NewsHour

JAMA article out ONLINE. Major favorable responses to roll-out. One recurrent issue is the skepticism of the community that as Trump administration would really do this. Also, there is no budget that is publicly out and so people are skeptical as to whether it will actually happen. All-in-all, very positive situation. I have been talking about this goal of ending the HIV epidemic in the USA for many years and some of the press are pointing that out. Much printed pres coverage. I had an acute attack this evening of norovirus with vomiting and diarrhea. Chris had the same thing starting onSaturday night in a restaurant when we went last weekend to Naples, FL to fish and stay with the Huskey’s. She is still not completely better. Hopefully this does not last long.
Had to stay home from work today and cancel our Winter Program Retreat due to nausea. Did telephone link to TV with WJLA Local Channel 9 on flu in the virgina, DC, Maryland area. Still widespread.

The CROI people, who rarely invite me to the meeting to talk now want me to give an Opening Session Plenary on the Ending HIV initiative in Seattle on Mar. 4. I will go. Continued intense print press about initiative, giving much credit to Bob Redfield and me.
Did BBC TV on Measles outbreaks; Also did Bloomberg TV News on the Ending HIV initiative. Did CSIS Filmed interview on HIV

Went to meeting in the Situation Room of the White House to meet with the NSC staff led by Charles Kupperman. Our HHS “team” led by Dep. Sec. Eric Hargan; also there were Bob Kadlec, Bob Redfield. NSC people were Jim Morrison and Lu Borio. Topic was the Executive Order of the POTUS on influenza and our preparedness. Eric had us put together a propose budget and plan of how HHS would fit into the plan in the Exec.Order. ASPR asked for $5.3 billion. I asked for $3.6 billion, mostly on universal influenza vaccine. Let us see if we get any money from this.

Did TV interview with Katy Kay of BBC on influenza. Also, did long (2 hours interview with Jon LaPook of CBS for the CBS Evening News tomorrow (Feb. 15) night and for a future “60 Minutes” segment, again on flu. The CBS interview did not air on Feb. 15 due to the Parkland, FL shooting and killing of 17 people.

Real busy (wall-to-wall) with meetings and preparations for upcoming Hearings on Ebola, measles, House and Senate Approps, and briefings on the Plan to End HIV Epidemic. Did BBC World Service Radio on our RCT for Ebola in DRC.

entries.content:
Had press briefing in “War Room” of Humphrey Building led by Secretary Azar including remarks on new information of interim vaccine efficacy (VE) discussed by Anne Schuchat and comments by Jerome Adams. Scott Gottlieb, Bob Kadlec and I were up on stage for questions, but there really were no questions. The issue is that the overall VE was 36% for all Influenzas; however, the VE for H3N2 was only 25%. Good news in that the overall VE for children 6 months to 8 years was 59% and for H3N2 was 51%.

Had dinner with Gary Nabel, Dabid Baltimore and his wife Alice Huang at San Lorenzo Restaurant in DC. Never been there before. This in anticipation of tomorrow when Gary, David, Nancy Messonnier (CDC) and I will do a session at the Annual AAAS meeting on Influenza.
